article_content: In Montana, a judge suggested that a 21-year-old, convicted of vandalism, should seek more gainful employment to expedite restitution payments. According to the Billings Gazette, District Judge G. Todd Baugh handed down a 10-year sentence, with half of it suspended, to Brandon Daniel Turell, also mandating over $13,000 in restitution. Judge Baugh is dealing with potential disciplinary action due to earlier statements about a rape victim appearing 'older than her chronological age.' Prosecutors noted that Turell and another person used a stolen BB gun back in December 2012 to damage the windows of approximately 100 vehicles. Turell pleaded guilty to felony criminal mischief, along with several misdemeanor charges like theft, theft by accountability, and DUI. 'I deeply regret my actions,' Turell told Judge Baugh. When Judge Baugh inquired about Turell's efforts to compensate victims, Turell mentioned working at Burger King. Judge Baugh responded by questioning why Turell couldn't secure a 'real job.' Turell stated he earned $9.50 per hour. Furthermore, Judge Baugh revoked Turell's previous sentence from 2009 for felony robbery and burglary charges. Turell was placed in the custody of the Department of Corrections until he turns 25 in 2018. At the conclusion of the hearing, a detention officer escorted Turell away in handcuffs.

article_content: Atlanta, Georgia (CNN) -- Want to increase your spending power? Consider shopping at a dollar store to give your wallet a break. Americans have increasingly turned to the four leading chains -- Dollar General, Family Dollar, Dollar Tree, and the 99¢ Only store -- during the recession. According to The New York Times, Dollar General's sales increased by nearly 10 percent quarter-over-quarter this year, and the company is opening 450 new stores. Dollar Tree, meanwhile, planned to open 235 new stores this year. Family Dollar's early 2009 numbers indicated a 6.5 percent year-over-year sales increase. However, despite the sales boom, Consumer Reports' Money Adviser has closely examined this popular retail sector and discovered that not all items offer a true bargain. Before I share their recommendations on what to buy and what to avoid, it's important to clarify the distinctions among the chains. Dollar General and Family Dollar primarily price their items at $1, but they also offer some merchandise at higher prices. Dollar Tree and the 99¢ Only chain are the only genuine dollar stores, where everything is priced at $1 without exception. So, what did Consumer Reports conclude? They found that cotton rounds, gift wrap, birthday candles, paper bags, composition notebooks, plastic cups, security envelopes, napkins, foam plates, and tissue paper are among the best deals. However, they advised against purchasing jewelry (due to high lead content), electrical products (potentially fake UL labels), medication (expired products), and vitamins (likely from non-reputable sellers) at any dollar store. I have personally bought medication like ibuprofen at dollar stores and have not encountered expired products. Some might argue that a better deal on ibuprofen can be found at a warehouse club. However, unless you're in constant pain, it's unlikely you'll use all those pills from a bulk container before they expire! The Consumer Reports research reminded me of a similar report published in Good Housekeeping several years ago. At that time, the magazine compared four generic products from dollar stores with four brand-name products purchased elsewhere. The products compared included generic glass cleaner, body lotion, dishwashing liquid, and detergent. The corresponding brand-name products were Windex, Lubriderm, Dawn, and Tide, which proved to be superior to their generic counterparts. For example, one teaspoon of Dawn washed 19 dishes, while a teaspoon of the dollar store brand washed only six! Regarding detergent, the dollar store brand failed to remove a mustard stain that Tide successfully removed. Therefore, it's crucial to exercise caution when shopping at dollar stores. While some good deals can be found, it's important to be selective.

Jepémo upéicha, ñemuvã ojejapóramo jepe, Consumer Reports' Money Adviser omaña porã ko ñemu rehe ha ohechakuaa ndaha'éiha opa mba'e iporã. Mba'e rehepa peẽ peñembo'y ha mba'érepa nahániri peñembo'y mboyve, tekotevẽ jahesape'a mba'éichapa ojoavy hikuái peteĩteĩ. Dollar Tree ha 99¢ Only añoite ha'e tenda añetegua 1 dólar rehegua, upépe opa mba'e ojehepyme'ẽ 1 dólarpe, ndaipóri mba'eve ohasáva upégui. Upéicharõ, mba'épa Consumer Reports oguahẽ? Ohechakuaa algodõ rehegua, kuatia ojepokuáva jopói rehe, vela aramboty rehegua, kuatia ryru, kuatiahaipyre, vaso plástico, kuatia ryru ojejokupyre, servilleta, plato espuma rehegua ha kuatia puku ojepokuáva ha'eha umi mba'e iporãvéva. Ha katu, ojerure ani haguã ojogua joya (orekoeterei plomo), tembiapo eletrisida rehegua (ikatu ndaha'éi marca UL añetegua), pohã (pohã okañymáva) ha vitamina (ikatu ndaha'éi umi ohepyme'ẽ añetegua) oimeraẽ tenda baratohápe. Che ajepokuaa ajogua pohã ibuprofen rehegua tenda baratohápe ha ndajuhúi mba'eve okañymáva. Oĩ ikatu he'íva iporãve hague ajogua ibuprofen peteĩ club mayorista-pe. Ha katu, nderasýi ramo mante, avave ndaikatumo'ãi oipuru opa umi pohã 12 millones oguerekóva ryru guasu okañy mboyve! Pe tembiapo Consumer Reports ojapo chemomandu'a peteĩ tembiapo ojoguaitereívape Good Housekeeping omosarambi hague ojapo heta ary. Upérõ, ko kuatiahaipyre kuñanguéra rehegua ombojojáva irundy tembiapo ndaha'éi marca añetegua rehegua tenda baratohápe irundy tembiapo marca añetegua rehegua ojejogua ambue hendápe. Umi tembiapo oñembojojáva ha'e ñemopotĩha vidrio rehegua, crema pire rehegua, pohãjovahéi y rehegua ha jabón. Umi tembiapo marca añetegua rehegua ha'e Windex, Lubriderm, Dawn, ha Tide, ha ojehechakuaa iporãve hague umi ndaha'éi marca añetegua reheguágui. Jabón rehegua, jabón ndaha'éi marca añetegua rehegua ndoipe'ái ky'a mostaza rehegua Tide ojapova'ekue. Upévare, tekotevẽ peñangareko pejogua jave tenda baratohápe. article_content: SINGAPORE: Singapore's economic growth is projected to improve in the second half of 2024 after facing an 'effective standstill' since late 2022, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) announced on Monday, Oct 30. MAS stated that Singapore is expected to benefit from the global tech industry's gradual recovery and the stabilization of global interest rates, according to its latest half-yearly macroeconomic review. The central bank also noted that growth rates across various sectors are trending towards their pre-COVID levels. The report indicated that 'For 2024, growth is projected to improve gradually in the second half of the year, approaching its potential rate for the year as a whole.' Economic growth for the current year is anticipated to be in the lower half of the 0.5 to 1.5 per cent forecast range.

MAS he'i oñeha'ãrõha Singapur operde provecho industria tecnológica global ñemoheñói jey mbeguekatúgui ha ñemopyenda porã interés kuéra global-pe, he'iháicha imarandu pyahu ipaha macroeconomic rehegua. Banco central he'i avei umi crecimiento tasa opaite sector-kuérape oñemohenda ohóvo umi nivel oguerekova'ekue pandemia mboyve. Marandu ohechauka 'Ary 2024-pe g̃uarã, crecimiento oñeproyecta omejora mbeguekatu segundo semestre ary-pe, og̃uahẽvo ipu'akaite ikatúvape ary pukukue javeve.' Crecimiento económico ko ary g̃uarã oñeha'ãrõ oĩ mbytépe pe 0,5 ha 1,5 por ciento rango-pe.

article_content: Alex Baker and Chris Rose, two graduates from Sheffield, are launching a unique enterprise: affordable space travel, albeit virtual, for individuals worldwide. Their company, SentIntoSpace.com, will offer low-cost missions into the stratosphere using helium balloons to carry lightweight items like personal photographs, billboard advertisements, and even cakes, at a significantly reduced price compared to NASA or Virgin Galactic flights. Their initial balloon prototype costs approximately £350 and includes a camera capable of transmitting images from the Earth's stratosphere. The 1.5kg capsule attached to the helium balloon can reach altitudes of up to 23 miles. It’s equipped with a built-in camera for capturing images high above the Earth, and can accommodate photos or advertisements. The capsule, about the size of a lunchbox, ascends to a height of 37.6km using a helium balloon. GPS coordinates are relayed to the user's mobile phone, and images can be remotely captured before the balloon deflates and the capsule descends via parachute. In a recent University of Sheffield campaign, the names of over 2,000 students, alumni, prospective students, and academics were sent into the stratosphere on a memory card aboard the balloon-assisted spacecraft. The students have refined their design, enabling space enthusiasts to send their own messages into orbit and capture personalized images for the same reasonable price. Baker and Rose first experimented with a homemade device in 2011, using a styrofoam box, a cheap camera, and a helium balloon. They monitored its progress using a GPS device that responded to phone calls with coordinate updates. To date, their balloon has reached altitudes exceeding 23 miles (37km), double the Armstrong limit, the altitude at which humans cannot survive without a pressurized environment. 'This hobby has truly captured people's attention,' Baker stated. 'Considering the $200 billion cost of the space shuttle program, achieving 37km for just £350 feels incredible and remarkably affordable.' While manned missions aren't currently planned, the team is continuously learning and setting new altitude records with each launch. They frequently gather at Baker's home in Sheffield, known as Mission Control, to improve their equipment. The capsule weighs slightly over 1.5kg, is roughly the size of a lunchbox, and ascends to altitudes of 37.6 kilometers before descending with a parachute after the balloon deflates. The University of Sheffield campaign utilized a memory card to carry the names of more than 2,000 university community members into the stratosphere. Rose explained, 'We are providing non-specialists with the tools for their own space missions. The setup is straightforward and easy to grasp. We even sent a cake into space for a web design company’s tenth anniversary, proving that anything light enough can be attached.' 'The highest we’ve reached is 23 miles, but we are optimistic about reaching even greater heights as technology advances.' SentIntoSpace.com is scheduled to launch in October, offering a standard kit for £350 that allows users to install their own video cameras and send messages or advertising campaigns. Rose added, 'The sky is the limit for us when we launch in October, and we are confident that our business will soar.' People can purchase starter kits from SentIntoSpace.com in October to send their own messages and photos. The standard kit costs £350 and accommodates user-installed video cameras. Currently, the students are focused on a 'Go Higher' campaign for the University of Sheffield, aiming to attract students to apply during the Clearing process. Baker commented, 'The University has produced numerous high achievers, including astronauts and Red Arrows pilots, making it fitting for us to launch a campaign centered around reaching for the stars.' Rose concluded, 'While we may not yet rival NASA or Virgin Galactic, we believe it’s only a matter of time. When you compare the $250,000 cost of a Virgin Galactic ticket to the cost of sending a picture of a loved one who’s dreamed of going to space, flying with us is a compelling option.'

Iñempréndape, SentIntoSpace.com, ome'ẽta viáhe hepykue michĩva estratósfera-pe oipurúvo globo de helio ogueraháva mba'e pohýikue'ỹva, techapyrãme ta'ãngakuéra personales, propagánda cartelkuérape, ha jepe pastelkuéra, peteĩ présio michĩvévape NASA térã Virgin Galactic viáhekuéragui. Pe cápsula 1.5kg orekóva oñemoĩva globo de helio-pe ikatu ohupyty yvatekue 23 millas peve. Oguereko peteĩ cámara oñemoĩmbáva ikatu haguã oñembohasa ta'ãngakuéra yvate Yvy ape árigui, ha ikatu ogueraha ta'ãngakuéra térã propagánda. Peteĩ campaña pyahu Universidad de Sheffield-pe, umi réra 2.000 estudiante, ex-alumno, potencial estudiante, ha académico-gua oñemondo estratósfera-pe peteĩ tarjeta de memoria ári pe nave espacial oipytyvõva globo rehe. Umi estudiante ojapoporãve idiseño, omoakãrapu'ãvo umi aficionado espacial-pe tomondo imarandu porã ha oipyhy hikuái ta'ãngakuéra ojejapova'ekue hendaitépe hepykue ndahasyiete guive. Baker ha Rose oñepyrũ va'ekue oha'ã peteĩ tembiporu ojejapova'ekue hógape 2011-pe, oipurúvo peteĩ caja de poliestireno, peteĩ cámara hepykue'ỹva, ha peteĩ globo de helio. Ojesareko hikuái iprogreso peteĩ tembiporu GPS rupive ombohováiva teléfono rupive oipyhývo umi coordenadas. Ágã peve, pe globo ohupyty yvatekue ohóva 23 millas (37km) ári, mokõi jey pe límite Armstrong, pe yvatekue yvypóra ndaikatúiva oiko peteĩ ambiente oñepresiona'ỹhápe. 'Kóva peteĩ afición añetehápe oipyhyva'ekue tapichakuérape,' Baker he'i. 'Ojesarekóvo pe $200 mil millones ogastáva'ekue programa transbordador espacial, ohupyty 37km péva £350 añónte rehe añetehápe ndahasyiete ha ikatupyryeterei.' Jepe umi misión tripulada noñeplanaĩri ko'áĝa, pe equipo oiko oñemoarandu ha ojapo récord pyahu yvatekuépe cada lanzamiento-pe. Py'ỹiete oñembyaty hikuái Baker rógape Sheffield-pe, ojekuaáva Mission Control-ramo, omoporãve haguã itembiporukuéra. Pe cápsula ohupyty pohýikue michĩmi 1.5kg ári, tuichakue peteĩ ryru tembi'úicha, ha ojupi yvatekue 37.6 kilómetros peve oguejy mboyve peteĩ paracaídas rehe pe globo ogue rire. Pe campaña Universidad de Sheffield oguerahava'ekue peteĩ tarjeta de memoria ombohasava'ekue umi réra 2.000 miembro comunidad universitaria-gua estratósfera-pe. Rose omyesakã, 'Ore rome'ẽ umi no especialistápe umi tembiporu imisión espacial-kuérape guarã. Pe montaje ndahasýi ha hasy'ỹnte oñentende. Rome'ẽ jepe peteĩ pastel espacio-pe peteĩ empresa diseño web oguerekóva diez años, jahechaukáva oimeraẽva mba'e pohýikue'ỹva ikatuha oñemoĩ. 'Pe yvateve roĝuahẽva'ekue ha'e 23 millas, ha ore rojerovia roĝuahẽtaha yvateve ko tecnología oñakãrapu'ãvo. SentIntoSpace.com oñepyrũta Octubre-pe, ome'ẽvo peteĩ kit estándar £350 rehe omoakãrapu'ãva umi usuario-pe omoĩ hikuái icámara video ha tomondo umi marandu porã térã campaña publicidad-gua. Rose ombojoapy, 'Yvága ha'e límite oreve guarã roñepyrũvo Octubre-pe, ha rojerovia ore empresa ohupytýtaha yvate. Umi tapicha ikatu ojogua umi kit ñepyrũrã SentIntoSpace.com-pe Octubre-pe tomondo imarandu porã ha ta'ãngakuéra. Pe kit estándar ogasta £350 ha omoakãrapu'ã umi cámara de vídeo oñemoĩva usuario rupive. Ko'áĝa, umi estudiante oñecentra peteĩ campaña 'Go Higher' Universidad de Sheffield-pe guarã, omoakãrapu'ãva umi estudiante-pe ojapo hikuái solicitud Clearings-pe. Baker ojerure, 'Pe Universidad oreko heta logro pyahu, umi astronauta ha piloto Red Arrows, omoha'ãva ore rombohape peteĩ campaña yvága rehe. Rose omohu'ã, 'Jepe ndoropu'akái gueteri NASA térã Virgin Galactic, rojerovia ha'e peteĩ asunto ára rehegua. Rejesarekóvo pe $250.000 ogastáva peteĩ pasaje Virgin Galactic-pe ha rembojojáva upe ogastáva remoĩvo peteĩ ta'ãnga nde sy térã nde rukuéra oikeraseva'ekue espacio-pe, reha'ã ramo orendive ha'e peteĩ jeiporavo porã.'

article_content: A Tennessee magistrate who ordered a baby's name changed from 'Messiah' to 'Martin' has been charged with violating the state's Code of Judicial Conduct. Child Support Magistrate Lu Ann Ballew ordered the name change during a paternity hearing in Newport on August 8. At the time, the parents, Jaleesa Martin and Jawaan McCullough, were disputing the 8-month-old baby's surname. The mother, Jaleesa Martin, wanted to keep the name she had given her son, Messiah Deshawn Martin, while the father, Jawaan McCullough, wanted the baby to bear his last name. Magistrate Ballew surprised both parents by ordering the baby's name to be changed to Martin Deshawn McCullough, stating that the name 'Messiah' was not in the baby's best interest. Her written order stated, ''Messiah' is a title that is held only by Jesus Christ.' 'Labeling this child 'Messiah' places an undue burden on him that, as a human being, he cannot fulfill,' the order continued. Ballew further stated that 'it is highly likely that he will offend many Cocke County citizens by calling himself 'Messiah',' but she proceeded with the name change anyway. That decision was overturned the following month in Cocke County Chancery Court, with the judge ruling that Ballew's decision violated the U.S. Constitution. Ms. Martin said, 'I was shocked. I never intended on naming my son Messiah because it means God, and I didn't think a judge could make me change my baby's name because of her religious beliefs.' The boy is now officially called Messiah DeShawn McCollough. The mother's two other children are named Micah and Mason, and she argued that she wanted to name her third child with an 'M' as well. According to the Social Security Administration's 2012 list of names, Messiah is ranked as the 387th most popular baby name. It was revealed that Magistrate Ballew initially ruled to keep the original name but then changed the written record and held a second hearing. On Wednesday, a panel of the Tennessee Board of Judicial Conduct filed formal charges against Ballew. The code requires that judges perform all duties without bias or prejudice based on religion. Ballew has 30 days to respond to the charges.

article_content: A young man, thought to be an undocumented immigrant, was discovered holding onto the underside of a recreational vehicle that had traveled from Calais to Kent. Sources indicate the individual, possibly in his late teens, attached himself to the vehicle's frame prior to its passage through the Channel Tunnel. After the two-hour trip, the stowaway was found as Paul Coles and his daughter, Joanne, were returning the vehicle in Ashford. Law enforcement responded to a call at the residence of Teresa Tyrer, who operates a motorhome rental business. The young man, reportedly in tears, was then transferred to immigration authorities. Tyrer mentioned that he appeared distressed and uncertain upon discovery. The Coles family had been driving since early morning to catch the crossing at Calais. Tyrer stated she had specifically cautioned the renters to secure the garage and avoid stopping at gas stations, citing concerns about potential harassment and the presence of individuals attempting to hitch rides to the UK. The young man, who did not speak English, was found by Mr. Coles while unloading motorcycles. According to reports, the suspected immigrant waited calmly on the grass while police arrived and took him into custody. Tyrer noted the young man, estimated to be around 17 years old, was crying as he was led away. He had clung to the vehicle for the entire 54-mile journey from France to Ashford. Mr. Coles immediately alerted his daughter to call the police upon discovering the stowaway. Tyrer recounted that the young man appeared shaken and unsure of what to do, and he sat quietly after the authorities were contacted. He was reportedly writing in Arabic on a piece of paper, the purpose of which was unknown. Tyrer acknowledged differing opinions on immigration but emphasized the individual's humanity. She stated that while she does not advocate for uncontrolled immigration, she recognized the young man's desperation and hoped he would not simply be sent back. A police spokesperson confirmed the incident, stating that they had responded to a call about a suspected illegal immigrant found under a motorhome and that the individual had been transferred to immigration enforcement. The Home Office has been contacted for further comment. Recent months have seen thousands of immigrants gather in Calais, establishing temporary settlements and seeking entry into the UK. Demonstrators have protested, asserting their human rights, while authorities struggle to prevent them from accessing ferries and vehicles bound for the UK.

article_content: During his tour in South Korea, Pope Francis met with women who were forced into sexual slavery by the Japanese military during World War II during a Mass. In a touching moment at the start of the service, Francis greeted seven women, many in wheelchairs, who are advocating for a renewed apology and compensation for their experiences. One of the women gave him a butterfly pin, a symbol of the 'comfort women's' plight, which he immediately pinned to his vestments and wore throughout the Mass. In his homily, Francis stated that reconciliation can only be achieved through forgiveness, even when it seems 'impossible, impractical, and even at times repugnant.' Prior to the start of a Mass of reconciliation at Seoul's main cathedral, Pope Francis met with these women. Francis urged the emergence of new opportunities for dialogue, encounter, and the resolution of differences, and for continued generosity in providing humanitarian assistance to those in need. He also hoped for an ever-greater recognition that all Koreans are brothers and sisters, members of one family, one people. The Pope received the butterfly pin from Kim Bok-dong, one of the 'comfort women' who attended his Mass. These elderly South Korean women, many of whom regularly participate in rallies and high-profile events, seek greater global attention as they urge Japan to apologize. In an interview before the Mass, Lee Yong-soo, another woman who often speaks to the media, expressed her hope that the meeting would provide some solace for the pain she and others still feel more than seven decades after their violation. Francis concluded his first trip to Asia by challenging Koreans, both North and South, to reject the 'mindset of suspicion and confrontation' that clouds their relations and to find new ways to forge peace on the war-divided peninsula. Historians estimate that 20,000 to 200,000 women from across Asia, many of them Korean, were forced to provide sex to Japanese soldiers. Japanese nationalists argue that the 'comfort women' in wartime brothels were voluntary prostitutes, not sex slaves, and that Japan has been unfairly criticized for a practice they claim is common in wartime. Many South Korean women have demanded a full apology with official government compensation. In 1995, Japan provided 2 million yen ($20,000) each to about 280 women in the Philippines, Taiwan, and South Korea through a private fund and funded nursing homes and medical assistance for Indonesian and former Dutch sex slaves. However, some survivors refused the money because it did not come directly from the government. Repeated wavering among senior right-wing politicians since the apology has contributed to a feeling in South Korea that Japan is in denial and not sufficiently remorseful. Before returning to Rome, the Pope held a Mass of reconciliation at Seoul's main cathedral, attended by South Korean President Park Geun-hye and some North Korean defectors. It was the final event of a five-day trip that highlighted the importance of Asia for the papacy and the Catholic Church, given its growth in Asia and decline in Europe. Francis's plea for peace coincided with joint military drills by the United States and South Korea, which North Korea warned would result in a 'merciless pre-emptive strike.' During his trip, the Pope reached out to China, North Korea, and other countries that lack relations with the Holy See. The Pope is scheduled to visit the Philippines and Sri Lanka in January. In Seoul on Monday, Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle stated that Francis is offering a 'friendly hand' to other countries, assuring them that the Church is not there for any worldly ambition or as conquerors, but as brothers and sisters. Francis established these themes from the start of his visit, which was marked by the firing of five rockets from Pyongyang into the sea. North Korea later claimed the test firings were unrelated to Francis's arrival and commemorated the 69th anniversary of Korea's independence from Japanese occupation. The U.S.-South Korean military exercises, involving tens of thousands of troops, are described by the allies as routine and defensive, but Pyongyang views them as preparation for invasion. A spokesman for the North Korean army's general staff stated that a 'most powerful and advanced merciless pre-emptive strike will start any time chosen by us.' Such rhetoric is typical from North Korea, and direct strikes are rare, although attacks blamed on the North in 2010 resulted in 50 South Korean deaths. Before the Mass, Seoul Cardinal Andrew Yeom Soo-jung dedicated a 'crown of thorns' made from barbed wire from the demilitarized zone separating the two Koreas to the Pope. 'Ut unum sint,' reads the inscription – 'that they may be one' – a phrase typically used when praying for unity among Catholics, Orthodox, and other Christians, but it takes on a new meaning in the Korean context. In his homily, Francis said that the Korean people know well the pain of division and conflict and urged them to reflect on how they could work to reconcile individually and as a people. He challenged them to reject a mindset shaped by suspicion, confrontation, and competition, and instead to cultivate a culture formed by the teachings of the Gospel and the noblest traditional values of the Korean people. When he was a young Jesuit, Francis had wanted to be a missionary in Asia but was prevented due to poor health. He used his trip to South Korea to encourage young Asians to embrace the missionary call to spread the faith. He also used the trip to console Koreans, meeting several times with relatives of victims of the Sewol ferry disaster, in which 300 people died. Throughout his trip, he wore a yellow pin given to him by the families.
translated_content: Oguata aja Corea del Sur rupi, Papa Francisco oñomongeta kuñanguéra ndive oikova'ekue esclavo sexual ramo umi militar japonés poguýpe Segunda Guerra Mundial aja peteĩ Misa aja. Peteĩ momento iporãitereívape servicio ñepyrũme, Francisco omomaitei pokõi kuñáme, heta oĩva apyka pohyime, ojerurevéva hikuái tojejerure perdón pyahu ha toñeme'ẽ indemnización umi mba'e ohasava'ekuére. Peteĩ kuña ome'ẽ chupe peteĩ prendedor mariposa rehegua, peteĩ techaukaha umi 'kuñanguéra oñembohováiva' rembiasakuére, ha'e omoĩpeteĩva'ekue ijaópe ha oipuru pukukue javeve Misa. Iñemongetahápe, Francisco he'i pe ñemoirũ jey ikatuha ojehupyty perdón rupive añónte, jepeve ojekuaa 'ndaikatúiha, ndojepuruhái ha sapy'ánte ivaíva'. Oñepyrũ mboyve peteĩ Misa de reconciliación Seúl tupão guasúpe, Papa Francisco oñomongeta ko'ã kuñanguéra ndive. Francisco ojerure tojeheka tape pyahu diálogo-pe guarã, joaju, ha toñesoluciona umi mba'e ojoavýva, ha toñeme'ẽve pytyvõ humanitario umi oikotevẽvape. Avei oha'ãrõ toñerekonoceve mayma coreano ha'eha joyke'y, peteĩ familia miembrokuéra, peteĩ tetãygua. Papa ohupyty pe prendedor mariposa rehegua Kim Bok-dong-gui, peteĩ umi 'kuñanguéra oñembohováiva' oúva'ekue imisa-pe. Ko'ã kuñakarai coreana del sur-gua, heta jey ojekuaáva aty guasu ha evento de alto perfil-pe, oheka atención global tuichavéva ojerure aja Japón tojerure perdón. Peteĩ entrevista ojejapo mboyve Misa, Lee Yong-soo, ambue kuña oñe'ẽ jepi prensa-pe, omombe'u oha'ãrõ pe jeju oipytyvõta michĩmi jepe pe hasýva gueteri oñandúva ha'e ha ambuekuéra setenta ary rire ojejapóma guive hesekuéra. Francisco omohu'ã iguata ypy Asia rupi ojerurévo coreanokuérape, norte ha sur-guápe, tomboyke pe 'apensa sospecha ha confrontación rehegua' omoypytũva iñemarã ha oheka tape pyahu ojejapo hag̃ua py'aguapy pe yvy pehẽ oñorairõva'ekuépe. Historiador-kuéra oestima 20.000 guive 200.000 kuñáme Asia tuichakuégui, hetave umi coreana, ojejopyva'ekue ome'ẽ hag̃ua sexo umi soldado japonés-pe. Umi nacionalista japonés he'i umi 'kuñanguéra oñembohováiva' umi burdel de guerra aja ha'ehague prostituta voluntaria, ndaha'éi esclavo sexual, ha oje'e hesekuéra oñecritica hague injustamente peteĩ mba'e ojejapo jepiha oñorairõ jave. Heta kuña coreana del sur-gua ojerure perdón completo ha toñeme'ẽ indemnización oficial gobierno guive. 1995-pe, Japón ome'ẽ 2 millones yen ($20.000) peteĩteĩ 280 kuñáme Filipinas, Taiwán ha Corea del Sur-pe peteĩ fondo privado rupive ha oipytyvõ hogar de anciano ha pohãnohárape umi esclavo sexual indonesia ha holandesa-kuérape. Umi superviviente katu omboyke pe pirapire ndogueruichéigui gobierno-gui. Jerure perdón rehegua oñembohasáva político de derecha-kuéra apytépe ojapóva ojehecha Corea del Sur-pe Japón ndoipotáiha ohechakuaa hembiapokue ha noñarrepentichéiha hekópe. Ojevy mboyve Roma-pe, Papa ojapo peteĩ Misa de reconciliación Seúl tupão guasúpe, oúva'ekue Presidente coreana del sur Park Geun-hye ha umi desertor coreano del norte. Ha'eva'ekue peteĩ evento paha peteĩ paseo de cinco días aja ohechaukáva mba'eichaitépa Asia iñimportante papado ha Iglesia Católica-pe guarã, ohechávo okakuaaha Asia-pe ha sa'iveha Europa-pe. Jerure py'aguapy Francisco ojegueroja umi ejercicio militar ojapóva Estados Unidos ha Corea del Sur ndive, Corea del Norte he'iva'ekue péicha ojehúta peteĩ 'ataque preventivo vaietereíva'. Iguata aja, Papa oñemboja China, Corea del Norte, ha umi tetã ndoguerekóiva joaju Santa Sede ndive. Papa ohohagua Filipinas ha Sri Lanka-pe jasyteĩme. Seúl-pe lunes-pe, Cardenal Luis Antonio Tagle he'iva'ekue Francisco ome'ẽha 'po pytyvõ' ambue tetãnguérape, oaseguráva Iglesia ndoúiha ko'ápe mba'e reíre térã conquistador ramo, sino joyke'ýramo. Francisco omoheñói ko'ã mba'e iguata ñepyrũguive, ojeguerohoryva'ekue umi cohete ombokapúva Pyongyang guive yguasúpe. Corea del Norte he'i upéi umi prueba ndojoguáiha Francisco rehenguére ha ojeguerohory pe 69 aniversario Corea isãsóva guive Japón poguýgui. Umi ejercicio militar Estados Unidos ha Corea del Sur ojapóva, hetave miles de tropas, oje'e rutinario ha oñedefende hag̃ua, Pyongyang katu ohecha preparación ramo ñorairõ guasúpe guarã. Peteĩ vocero ejército coreano del norte-gua he'iva'ekue peteĩ declaración rupive 'ataque preventivo ipu'akapáva ha ipya'evéva oñepyrũta roiporavóva guive'. Ko'ãichagua ñe'ẽ Japón-gui ojehecha jepi, ha umi ñorairõ ndojejapói, jepeve umi ñorairõ oje'éva Corea del Norte ojapo hague 2010-pe ojuka 50 coreano del sur-guápe. Ojejapo mboyve pe Misa, Cardenal Andrew Yeom Soo-jung Seúl-gua ome'ẽ 'corona de espinas' Papa-pe ojejapóva alambre de púas-gui ojeguerúva pe yvy pehẽ oñemboja'óva umi Corea-kuérape. 'Ut unum sint,' he'i inscripción – 'ha'e guive peteĩta hikuái' – peteĩ ñe'ẽ ojeipurúva jepi oñembo'e jave católico, ortodoxo ha cristiano apytépe, katu oguereko peteĩ he'ise pyahu contexto coreano-pe. Iñemongetahápe, Francisco he'i pueblo coreano oikuaaporãha mba'eichaitépa hasy pe jeja'o ha pe ñorairõ ha ojerure chupekuéra toñepy'amongeta mba'éichapa ikatu omba'apo oñemoĩ jey hag̃ua peteĩteĩ ha pueblo ramo. Ojerure chupekuéra tomboyke apensa sospecha, confrontación ha competencia rehegua, ha en cambio tomongakuaa peteĩ cultura oñemopyendáva Evangelio mbo'epýre ha umi mba'e porãita pueblo coreano-pegua. Imitãrusúpe, Francisco oikoséva'ekue misionero ramo Asia-pe katu ndohoichéi hasykatúgui. Oipuru iguata Corea del Sur rupi omokyre'ỹvo umi Asia-gua mitãrusúpe toñemoĩ hikuái misionero ramo omyasãi hag̃ua fe. Avei oipuru iguata omokyre'ỹvo coreanokuérape, oñomongetávo jepi umi hénte omanóva familiar-kuéra ndive umi accidente Sewol-pe, omano haguépe 300 tapicha. Iguata pukukue javeve, oipuru peteĩ prendedor sa'yjuky opoíva umi familia.

article_content: Charlotte Joines, a mother of three, defied early criticism about her body size to achieve her ambition of becoming a model. Despite being told at age 22 that she was too large for modeling contracts due to her size eight figure, Charlotte persevered. A decade later, she realized her aspiration by becoming a swimwear model, even though she now wears a size 12. Charlotte's journey involved an initial rejection from agencies who considered her 'too big'. She recalls surviving on a restrictive diet and intense gym routine, which ultimately left her feeling drained and irritable, especially as a young mother. Inspired by her boyfriend, Floyd's, attention to other women in magazines, Charlotte aimed to provide him with an alternative focus. She pursued modeling, but faced repeated setbacks from agencies. These rejections chipped away at her confidence, despite being told that such experiences were typical in the industry. The turning point came when Charlotte and her friends—Camilla Andersen, Ellesha Newton, and Rufaro Nyakatawa—entered a competition to represent Curvy Kate. They were selected as winners by singer Sarah Harding and photographer Dan Kennedy. This victory led to a bikini photo shoot in Ibiza, just four months after Charlotte gave birth. Now 32, Charlotte emphasizes her improved self-assurance and happiness. She believes her newfound confidence was instrumental in achieving her modeling dream. Participating in the Curvy Kate competition with her friends offered a surprising opportunity for connection and support. The group's initial disbelief at reaching the finals turned into elation when they won a shoot in Ibiza. Charlotte highlights the importance of self-acceptance, noting that 'being a size eight isn’t everything; just do what makes you happy.' The Curvy Kate experience reinforced the idea that happiness isn't contingent on size.

article_content: In London, England, a sixteen-year-old schoolgirl from Australia aspires to accomplish a formidable sailing achievement that has pushed many seasoned sailors to their limits. Jessica Watson, aged sixteen and hailing from Australia, intends to undertake a solo sailing voyage around the globe. Jessica Watson, who resides in Mooloolaba, Queensland, is scheduled to embark on her solo circumnavigation in November, aiming to become the youngest individual to ever complete a non-stop, solo sail around the world. However, the prospect of weeks of solitude, reliance on freeze-dried meals, unpredictable weather conditions, and the potential for injury, illness, or even death raises the question: why would she pursue such a challenge? Watson revealed to CNN that she draws inspiration from fellow Australian Kay Cottee, the pioneering woman who sailed around the world alone without any stops, and Jesse Martin, an Australian originally from Germany, who still holds the record as the youngest person to accomplish this feat. Martin completed his voyage in 1999 at the age of 18 and later authored a book titled 'Lionheart: A Journey of the Human Spirit.' 'I read Jesse's book, and it was truly inspiring. If I had to pinpoint one thing that motivated me to do this, that would be it,' Watson explained. Since deciding to take on what she considers the 'Everest of the ocean' approximately four years ago, Watson has dedicated herself to preparing for the adventure as thoroughly as possible. She has already completed a 'mock solo' journey across the Tasman Sea, situated between Australia and New Zealand, at the age of 15 and has been sailing since she was eight. 'I've spoken with others [who've undertaken similar voyages] about their experiences, and I plan to accumulate a significant number of solo sailing miles before I depart,' she stated. Despite her accumulated experience, Watson acknowledges that some aspects of the journey remain uncertain. 'There are definitely things that make me nervous, such as the massive waves and equipment malfunctions. However, it's remarkable how much preparation we can achieve and what technology can offer.' 'Nevertheless, there's no way to know how you'll truly cope when you're out there for eight months until you're actually doing it.' Watson's circumnavigation aligns with a growing trend among young sailors. Mike Perham, a seventeen-year-old Briton, is currently in the midst of his solo, charitable sailing attempt around the world. Perham is presently held up in Tasmania, Australia, due to equipment problems and faces the daunting task of navigating around Cape Horn during the winter season. Despite these challenges, he has made substantial progress, especially considering the initial concerns surrounding his voyage. On his blog, Perham shares the trials of being alone at sea, stating, 'The initial days at sea are always the most difficult; the lack of sleep leaves me constantly exhausted, but I know I need to persevere, knowing that I'll soon adapt and things will steadily improve.' Another teenager, Zac Sunderland, 16, from California, also aims to become the youngest sailor to achieve this accomplishment. Sunderland has also progressed from his starting point in California, through the Panama Canal, and into the Atlantic Ocean. The availability of advanced communications technology has been crucial in persuading the parents of Perham, Sunderland, and Watson to allow them to embark on their voyages. On Sunderland's website, his father, Laurence, commented, 'Although Zac is sailing alone, he receives a great deal of support. Some will undoubtedly disagree with our decision to allow Zac to undertake this trip. It was his idea, and it is his desire to continue.' Watson noted that her parents have also been consistently supportive. For the young sailor, the immediate priorities include preparing her boat for departure and securing a final sponsor to help finance the voyage. She emphasized that her life is primarily centered around this challenge for the year ahead. 'It might take me a little longer to finish school... this adventure is putting everything else on hold.'

article_content: By Michael Zennie and Reuters. Federal judges struck down gay marriage bans in Indiana and Utah today in rulings that granted significant victories for same-sex couples and could affect four other states that currently ban such unions. In Indiana, a judge overturned the state's prohibition on gay marriage and ordered county clerks to immediately begin issuing marriage licenses to same-sex couples. The ruling against Utah, one of the most conservative states in the nation, was more sweeping, although less immediate. The 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver, in ruling against Utah's gay marriage ban, stated that states cannot ban same-sex unions because they are protected under the 14th Amendment of the Constitution, which guarantees equal protection under the law. Indiana has begun issuing marriage licenses to same-sex couples, while Utah's constitutional ban on gay marriage remains in place, pending appeal. Craig Bowen and Jake Miller kiss after being married by Marion County Clerk Beth White in Indianapolis following the federal judge's ruling. Erin Lynae Fox kisses Jennifer Elizabeth Fox as their sons Isaac, 7, and Redmond, 4, look on following their wedding in Indianapolis. The ruling affects six states in the 10th Circuit: Colorado, Kansas, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Utah, and Wyoming, potentially making such prohibitions illegal there, too. New Mexico already allows gay marriage, but the remaining states have laws prohibiting it. However, the three-judge panel immediately put their ruling on hold pending appeal, which the Utah Attorney General has promised to file. The next step is for the U.S. Supreme Court to take up the issue again. 'A state may not deny the issuance of a marriage license to two persons, or refuse to recognize their marriage, based solely upon the sex of the persons in the marriage union,' the 10th Circuit said in its 2-1 ruling on Utah. Supporters of gay marriage in the conservative state, where the Mormon church wields substantial political and social influence, planned a celebratory rally on Wednesday night in Salt Lake City. Utah briefly became the 18th U.S. state where marriage rights were extended to same-sex couples when a federal district judge ruled in December 2013 that the state ban on gay matrimony was unconstitutional. That decision was put on hold by the U.S. Supreme Court pending appeals, but not before more than 1,300 gay and lesbian couples married. From left, plaintiffs Moudi Sbeity, Derek Kitchen, Laurie Wood, and Kody Partridge, two of the three couples who brought the lawsuit against Utah's gay marriage ban, stand together at a news conference outside their lawyer's office in Salt Lake City. Sarah Perfetti and Abby Henkel are married outside the Monroe County Justice Building on Wednesday in Bloomington, Indiana. Utah lawmakers who oppose gay marriage had argued that the state's ban, known as Amendment 3, was approved by voters and that same-sex marriages were relatively new, so evidence about their impact on families might not be fully known. But the court said the state could not restrict the right to marry, or its recognition of marriage, 'based on compliance with any set of parenting roles, or even parenting quality.' 'We cannot embrace the contention that children raised by opposite-sex parents fare better than children raised by same-sex parents,' it said in its ruling. Separately, U.S. District Judge Richard Young in Indianapolis said Indiana's ban on same-sex marriage violated the Constitution's due process and equal protection clauses, and he ordered officials to start issuing marriage licenses. And a legal battle over Florida's gay marriage ban intensified this week as state Attorney General Pam Bondi said she will defend the measures approved by voters in 2008 in challenges to be heard soon in Orlando and Miami Beach. Indiana Attorney General Greg Zoeller has promised to appeal the ruling and asked the judge to stay his ruling and halt gay marriage in Indiana, pending the appeal.

article_content: The inspiration for Paddington Bear's home in Peru, before his travels to London, has been identified. Guests at the Inkaterra Andean Bear Sanctuary in Machu Picchu can encounter spectacled bears, the real-life inspiration for the children's character, in their native country. This luxury eco-hotel offers visitors a chance to learn about the relatives of the beloved character, known for his fondness for marmalade and duffle coats. Spectacled bears in Peru are critically endangered and are the only living bear species native to South America. Fans can experience Paddington Bear's connection to Peru through a hotel stay. A still from the movie 'Paddington' suggests the character's roots are in Peru. Guests can interact with spectacled bears before the release of the 'Paddington' movie. The sanctuary houses five Andean spectacled bears, offering travelers an opportunity to get close to this endangered species. Following time spent with the bears, guests can enjoy the luxury of the eco-hotel. The Andean Spectacled Bear Package starts at approximately £620 per guest. Visitors are given exclusive access to the enclosure and can shadow bear keepers to understand how the sanctuary aids the species' survival. Carmen Soto, Inkaterra's resident naturalist, notes the gradual destruction of the Andean spectacled bear's natural habitat due to agricultural development and increasing human population in the Andes Mountains. The hotel features a rainforest-themed bathroom and a spa pool. Soto emphasizes the danger of extinction faced by South America's only bear species. 'We hope our continued work, including the Andean spectacled bear package, will raise international awareness and help save this endangered species,' says Soto. The unique package includes a three-night stay at the Inkaterra Machu Picchu Hotel, where guests learn about the life of a bear keeper at the Andean spectacled bear project. A 'bear kit,' including a Bear Keeper's certificate and a soft toy spectacled bear, is provided to guests. The hotel offers guests the opportunity to observe the bears in a natural habitat. Guests will learn about the sanctuary's efforts to help the bear species thrive. A portion of the proceeds from the Andean Spectacled Bear Package will be donated to the Inkaterra Machu Picchu Spectacled Bear Sanctuary Project, and a guided tour of the Machu Picchu Citadel is included.

article_content: John Henson, the 48-year-old son of the legendary Jim Henson, the creative force behind children's entertainment, has died. According to a statement from his family's company, his death was caused by a 'sudden, massive heart attack'. The Jim Henson Company announced his passing on Facebook this past Saturday. The post indicated that he passed away on Friday at his home, surrounded by one of his two daughters. John Henson is survived by his wife, Gyongyi, in addition to his sisters and brothers, Lisa, Cheryl, Brian, and Heather. Two other members of his family occupy prominent leadership positions within the Jim Henson Company; Brian Henson holds the title of chairman, and Lisa Henson serves as CEO. The company's website prominently features John Henson as one of the five 'Henson family' members. He also held roles as a shareholder and board member. According to imdb.com, John Henson was involved in the family business in the 1980s, 1990s, and 2000s. His performance as Sweetums, the big, lovable character in 'The Muppets,' is particularly notable. His father, Jim, passed away unexpectedly in 1990. Jim was celebrated for launching popular shows like 'The Muppets' and 'Fraggle Rock,' and for creating iconic 'Sesame Street' characters, including Big Bird and Cookie Monster. Last April, John's mother, Jane Nabel Henson, died at the age of 79 after a battle with cancer. Jane had met Jim at the University of Maryland in 1954 during a puppetry class, and they married five years later. Currently, The Jim Henson Company continues to produce fantasy and science fiction productions, alongside animated children's shows such as 'Sid the Science Kid' and 'Dinosaur Train.'

article_content: During a routine surgery at Maidstone Hospital, Mike Wilcock, a 58-year-old health and safety inspector, sustained severe burns due to staff's improper use of an electric blanket, known as a 'hot dog'. The Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust has admitted to a breach of duty under the 1974 Health and Safety Act and could face a significant fine. The incident occurred because of insufficient training on the equipment; a cold saline bag touching a sensor caused the equipment's temperature to escalate rapidly. The burns left Mr. Wilcock with permanent scars, mobility problems, and four months of unemployment; he is now pursuing a legal claim. The hospital trust had previously breached safety protocols related to the device, including inadequate training and a failure to thoroughly investigate earlier incidents. The trust's medical director offered a formal apology to Mr. and Mrs. Wilcock regarding the incident. Mr. Wilcock voiced concerns about the potential for similar incidents in other hospitals using the same type of equipment. The trust has discontinued the use of the 'hot dog' equipment and maintains it was not introduced as a cost-cutting strategy. The judge expressed his regret and will determine the fine amount at a future hearing.

article_content: In an interview, Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice asserted that despite President Bush's low approval ratings, people will eventually 'start to thank this president for what he's done.' Rice stated, 'There is no greater honor than to serve this country.' She added, 'This president has faced tougher circumstances than perhaps at any time since the end of World War II, and he has delivered policies that are going to stand the test of time.' These remarks were made during an interview that aired on CBS' 'Sunday Morning.' The Secretary of State downplayed reports suggesting a decline in the United States' image internationally. She highlighted the administration's success in reshaping discussions in the Middle East. 'This isn't a popularity contest,' Rice emphasized. 'The administration's responsibility is to make sound decisions regarding Americans' long-term interests and values – focusing on historical impact rather than immediate headlines.' She continued, 'I am quite certain that when the final assessment is made, the removal of Saddam Hussein's Iraq, replaced by an Iraq that contributes positively to the future of the Middle East, will be viewed favorably. Likewise, the improved U.S.-China and U.S.-India relationships, along with stronger ties with Brazil and other Latin American nations, will be recognized.' 'Considering our accomplishments in fostering discussions about democracy and values in the Middle East, this administration will be judged favorably. I prefer to await history's assessment rather than be swayed by current news,' she added. When CBS' Rita Braver questioned Rice about claims from former diplomats that Americans are disliked globally, Rice responded, 'That's simply not accurate.' 'I am aware of the achievements of U.S. policy. I am uncertain which diplomats you are referring to; however, the record speaks for itself,' she stated. Rice indicated that she is unfazed by criticism directed at her or the administration's policies, explaining that a lack of criticism would suggest a failure to take meaningful action. 'I'm here to make tough choices, and this president is here to make tough choices, and we have. And yes, there are some things that I would do very differently if I had it to do over again. You don't have that luxury. You have to make the choices and take the positions that you do at the time,' she said. Regarding historians who consider Bush to be among the worst presidents, Rice countered that those 'aren't very good historians.' 'Making historical judgments before an administration has concluded its term, or while the future of the Middle East remains uncertain, and before evaluating the full impact of the President's decisions on the region, is premature. Good historians are still writing about George Washington and Harry Truman,' she elaborated. Rice, aged 54, expressed her enjoyment of serving in the Bush administration for the past eight years, initially as national security advisor and subsequently as secretary of state. 'There is no greater honor than to serve this country,' she remarked, while also acknowledging the immense challenge involved. Rice disclosed her plans to return to the Hoover Institution at Stanford University following the change in administration, where she intends to write two books: one focusing on foreign policy and the other on her parents.

article_content: Bayern Munich secured a comfortable 2-0 victory against Borussia Monchengladbach at Borussia Park on Friday, marking the Bundesliga's return after the winter break. Following a 3-0 defeat to Red Bull Salzburg in a friendly last weekend, Pep Guardiola urged his team to reignite their passion, a call they answered against the league's third-placed team. Any apprehension among Bayern's traveling fans was quickly dispelled when Mario Gotze scored in the seventh minute, converting Thomas Muller's cut-back with a low, first-time shot. Despite controlling possession for the majority of the first half, Bayern couldn't extend their lead until after halftime. Granit Xhaka's clear handball in the 52nd minute resulted in a penalty for Bayern, which Thomas Muller converted, sending Marc-Andre ter Stegen the wrong way to double their advantage. Gladbach responded immediately, attempting to reduce the deficit. Patrick Herrmann's shot hit the post in the 63rd minute, and he later scuffed another attempt after being set up by Raffael two minutes later. However, Bayern continued to dictate the game, maintaining approximately two-thirds of possession. In the final ten minutes, Arjen Robben made his comeback, returning to the field after a six-week absence due to a knee injury sustained in December. This win brings Bayern to 47 points, a ten-point lead over second-place Leverkusen. Sami Hyypia's team will travel to Freiburg on Saturday, while Borussia Dortmund, in fourth place, can overtake Monchengladbach if they defeat Augsburg at the Westfalenstadion.

article_content: In Orlando, Florida, a hearing took place Friday where one of Casey Anthony's lawyers described the prosecution's attempt to bill her over $516,000 for investigation expenses as petty, considering she wasn't found guilty of murdering her daughter. Prosecutors argue they're entitled to repayment because Anthony was convicted of four counts of misleading investigators following the disappearance of her daughter, Caylee, in 2008. However, defense attorney J. Cheney Mason argued this bill is unjust after Anthony's acquittal on the more serious murder charge. 'What about fairness for the defense that prevailed?' Mason questioned Judge Belvin Perry Jr. of Orange County. 'Are we now going to be penalized again... paying for everything they did, including their travels, meals, books, and experts, which had no connection to the crimes she was convicted of?' Prosecutor Linda Drane Burdick told Perry he should approve the reimbursement request. 'The defense's argument misses the key point regarding prosecution costs,' she stated. 'If Ms. Anthony hadn't lied to law enforcement at the start of this investigation, these costs wouldn't exist.' Perry didn't immediately rule on the request after Friday's extensive hearing, which Anthony didn't attend. He plans to review legal briefs and research the law before making a decision. The Florida Department of Corrections released a statement Friday saying Anthony met with her probation officer on Thursday, as required by her sentence following her 2010 conviction for check fraud. Anthony reported she's unemployed, hasn't earned any income in the last month, and isn't enrolled in any classes. The department noted 'No violations have been identified' regarding Anthony's probation, which includes restrictions on drug use and excessive alcohol consumption. This meeting was held privately because Anthony has remained secluded since her release from prison in July after being acquitted in the 2008 death of her two-year-old daughter. Corrections officials have kept her location private due to safety concerns. Caylee Anthony's skeletal remains were discovered in December 2008 in a wooded area near her home. Anthony's lawyers admitted she lied to authorities during the search for her daughter, saying she knew Caylee was deceased. Her lawyers have claimed Caylee's death was an accident. Prosecutors are seeking reimbursement under a Florida law allowing the state to fine defendants to recover costs. Court documents show the Orange County Sheriff's Office spent $293,123.77 on the case, while the District Attorney's Office spent at least $140,390.60. The Florida Department of Law Enforcement spent $71,939.56, and the Metropolitan Bureau of Investigation spent $10,645.38. Mason argued that prosecutors are seeking reimbursement for expenses unrelated to the crimes she was convicted of. He suggested that if Perry finds merit in the state's motion, he should limit expenses to costs specifically related to the search for Caylee Anthony.

article_content: A study funded by Cancer Research UK suggests that appealing cigarette packaging motivates young individuals who have never smoked to begin the habit. The research indicated that youngsters favored innovative packaging designs over plain ones. This follows earlier research from the University of Stirling indicating that graphic warnings on cigarette packs had minimal effect on adolescent smokers. The study found that attractive cigarette packaging tempts young people to start smoking, whereas plain packaging discourages them. The ability of teenagers to recall images of diseased lungs, rotten teeth, and neck cancer was less than 10 percent. Written warnings without images were recalled by less than one percent of over 1,000 teenagers. The new research, published in BMJ Open, examined the reactions of 1,025 UK children aged 11 to 16 who had never smoked. They were given regular, novelty, and plain cigarette packs. Novelty packs featured unusual shapes, colors, or opening systems, while standardized packs were brown and devoid of branding except for the brand name. Researchers discovered that children preferred the vibrant and novelty packs from leading manufacturers, such as Silk Cut Superslim's slim pack, the Marlborough Bright Leaf pack that opens like a Zippo lighter, and Pall Mall's pink pack. Children who liked these packs were more likely to be tempted to smoke. For example, individuals receptive to the Silk Cut pack were over four times more likely to be susceptible to smoking. In contrast, plain packaging reduced the appeal of smoking. After the government postponed plans to introduce plain cigarette packaging, it denied claims that it had given in to the tobacco industry. The decision was delayed to allow further examination of similar initiatives in Australia. Cancer Research UK stated that the delay allows the tobacco industry to profit from attractive packs that recruit new smokers. Almost 570 children under 16 start smoking in the UK every day. Dr. Harpal Kumar, chief executive of Cancer Research UK, stated that this study provides more evidence that appealing packaging increases the likelihood that children will try their first cigarette, leading to a deadly addiction that will kill half of them if they become long-term smokers. He urged the government to protect children from sophisticated marketing and prioritize the health of young people over the tobacco industry's profits. He advocated for the introduction of plain packaging to reduce youth smoking. Professor Gerard Hastings, a social marketing expert, added that this research strengthens the case for protecting children from the tobacco industry's marketing. He stated that the UK should follow Australia's example and introduce plain packaging immediately. He also cautioned against overlooking the industry's potential to develop new marketing strategies within the pack, such as special coatings. He concluded that the tobacco industry is desperately using any means to sell its products and secure profits from future smokers and emphasized the need to de-glamorize this deadly habit.
translated_content: Peteĩ estudio oñefondeáva Cancer Research UK rupive ohechauka umi cigarrillo empaqueta iporãva omokyre'ỹha umi mitãrusu araka'eve noipytyvõiva'ekue opita haguã oñepyrũ haguã pe vicio. Pe investigación ohechauka mitãrusukuéra oguerohoryveha umi diseño empaqueta innovador-kuéra umi paquete simple ári. Kóva oúvo peteĩ investigación ymaveguágui Universidad de Stirling pegua ohechaukáva umi advertencia gráfica umi cigarrillo paquete ári michĩmi mba'e ojapo umi mitãrusu pitador ári. Pe estudio ojuhu umi cigarrillo empaqueta iporãva oipytyvõha mitãrusukuérape oñepyrũ haguã opita, ha umi paquete simple katu omboyke chupekuéra. Pe katupyry oguereko mitãrusukuéra imandu'a haguã ta'anga pulmón hasývagui, tãi kangue ha cáncer ajúgui ndohupytýi 10 por ciento. Umi advertencia ojehaíva ta'anga'ỹre katu ndojemandu'ái ni 1 por ciento umi 1.000 rupi mitãrusúgui. Pe investigación pyahu, oñepublicáva BMJ Open-pe, ohesa'ỹijo umi reacción oguereko 1.025 mitã UK pegua orekóva 11 ha 16 ary ndopitáiva'ekue araka'eve. Oñeme'ẽ chupekuéra cigarrillo paquete regular, novedad ha simple. Umi investigador ojuhu mitãkuéra oguerohoryveha umi paquete vibrante ha novedad umi fabricante principal-kuéragui, techapyrã Silk Cut Superslim paquete delgado, Marlborough Bright Leaf paquete ojeavríva peteĩ encendedor Zippo-icha, ha Pall Mall paquete rosado. Mitãkuérape ogustáva ko'ã paquete oĩporãve opita haguã. Techapyrãme, umi persona oĩporãva Silk Cut paquete-pe oĩ irundy vése iporãvéva oñentregávo pitápe. Kóvaicha, umi paquete simple omboguejy pe interése opita haguã. Gobierno omboyke rire plan omoinge haguã paquete cigarrillo simple, omboyke avei umi ñe'ẽ oñentregávo industria tabacalera-pe. Pe decisión oñemboguejyve ikatu haguã ojehecha porãve umi iniciativa ojoguáva Australia-pe. Cancer Research UK he'i ko demora omoĩha industria tabacalera-pe oganáva umi paquete iporãvágui orekrutáva pitador pyahúpe. Haimete 570 mitã 16 ary guýpe oñepyrũ opita Reino Unido-pe ára ha ára. Dr. Harpal Kumar, jefe ejecutivo Cancer Research UK pegua, he'i ko estudio ome'ẽha evidencia iporãvéva umi paquete iporãva ombohetaveha umi mitã oha'ãtava pe cigarrillo peteĩha, ogueraháva peteĩ vicio mortífera ojuka vaerã hetãguágui haimete. Ojerure gobierno-pe oproteje haguã mitãkuérape umi marketing sofisticado-gui ha tomoĩ tenonde umi mitãrusu resãi industria tabacalera ganancia ári.  Ojerure avei toñemoinge paquete simple omboguejy haguã umi mitãrusu opitáva. Profesor Gerard Hastings, experto marketing social pegua, omyesakã avei ko investigación omombareteveha pe káso oproteje haguã mitãkuérape umi industria tabacalera marketing-gui.  He'i Reino Unido osegui vaerãha Australia ejemplo ha omoinge paquete simple pya'e voi. Avei oalertaa ani haguã ojeheja rei industria ikatúha omoheñói estrategia pyahu paquete pype, techapyrã recubrimiento especial. Omohu'ã industria tabacalera oipurúha desesperadamente opaite mba'e ikatúva ovende haguã iproducto ha ogana umi pitador futurogui ha ojerure tojejora hağuã ko vicio ivaívagui.

article_content: Police are investigating the death of a three-year-old girl who was fatally injured when a fireplace surround collapsed on her. The incident occurred inside a family home in Plymouth, Devon, where the fireplace surround toppled onto the child, causing severe head injuries. Emergency services, including police, fire, and ambulance crews, were dispatched to the scene. The girl was rushed to Derriford Hospital in Plymouth, but was pronounced dead upon arrival. Authorities are treating the incident as a tragic accident and are considering potential health and safety violations. Devon and Cornwall Police confirmed they received a 999 call at 4:35 pm on Sunday reporting the collapse of the fireplace surround. A police spokesman stated that the girl sustained serious head injuries and received treatment at the scene before being transported to Derriford Hospital, where she later died. The incident has deeply affected residents in Colebrook, a community on the outskirts of Plymouth. Officers remain at the family home to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident; the child's name has not been released. Jane Tadman, landlady of the Colebrook Inn, recounted the arrival of emergency services and the community's shock upon learning the news, expressing sympathy for the family. The South Western Ambulance Service reported receiving a call at approximately 4:30 pm on Sunday and dispatching medical personnel, including a doctor and ambulance crews. They conveyed the child to Derriford Hospital in critical condition and extended condolences to the family. The Health and Safety Executive is aware of the incident, but Devon and Cornwall Police are leading the investigation.

article_content: After Haiti's devastating earthquake, Georges Nader carefully retrieved Hector Hyppolite's oil-on-cardboard painting, treating it with the tenderness a father would show a wounded child, barely holding back tears. 'Vase et Fleurs,' a masterpiece of art naif simplicity, was fragmented like a complex jigsaw puzzle. Some pieces were tattered, others missing altogether. Like much else in Haiti, the painting by one of the country's leading artists was lost, a masterpiece gone, taking with it a piece of Haiti's history. Nader, sifting through the rubble of a demolished museum in Port-au-Prince that once housed his family's collection of 12,000 artworks, believed no one could ever reassemble it. Each piece chronicled the history and aspirations of a people who endured hardship and expressed themselves through painting and sculpture. Lacking the established institutions, buildings, and monuments of wealthier nations, Haiti relied on depictions of sun, sea, people, and animals by untrained artists—some incorporating spiritual traditions of voodoo culture—to serve as its collective memory. Hyppolite, a voodoo priest and self-taught artist, used his fingers and brushes crafted from chicken feathers to paint. This Friday, Nader will again stand before Hyppolite's 1946 still life, its vibrant colors revitalized by conservators in collaboration with the Smithsonian Institution. Nader expressed his wonder, calling it 'a miracle.' The painting is one of two restored artworks featured in a larger exhibition of 50 pieces by Haitian artists. The other rescued piece is 'Beau Reve' by Celestin Faustin. 'Saving Grace: A Celebration of Haitian Art,' organized by Affirmation Arts and curated by prominent Haitian art historian Gerald Alexis, holds profound significance for Alexis and Nader. It stands as a potent symbol of Haiti's rebirth, especially given criticisms of slow recovery efforts after the earthquake. Alexis emphasized that this represents the identity of the Haitian people. He stated that neglecting it would deprive future generations of their heritage, making it a duty to preserve. In the earthquake's immediate aftermath, Nader and other Haitian art collectors salvaged thousands of artworks from the debris, preventing their permanent loss. In a single room of his museum, he rescued 1,000 pieces, with 70 percent requiring restoration. Quantifying the loss was challenging, Nader noted, because Haiti lacked the extensive network of museums and galleries found in the United States. Much of the nation's cultural wealth resided in private homes and collections, like his father's, which began decades earlier. The total number of lost pieces remained uncertain. As the second floor of his gallery transformed into an art hospital, Nader resolved to restore every piece. He and Alexis began contacting experts, initiating a search for individuals with the expertise to perform delicate restoration work. They partnered with the Smithsonian, leading to the establishment of the Cultural Recovery Centre in collaboration with the Haitian government in the hills of Port-au-Prince. Haiti's cultural heritage, like Africa's endangered lions, needed protection, which became the center's mission. Richard Kurin, under-secretary for history, art and culture at the Smithsonian, deemed it unconscionable to abandon the art beneath the rubble. He described the recovery center as 'magically' restoring thousands of damaged pieces and also training Haitians in conservation techniques. A September course instructed 26 participants on identifying deterioration agents, providing first aid treatment, preparing for emergencies, and creating safe storage for collections. Kurin sees the restoration of art as the restoration of hope, giving people access to their heritage by restoring the past. Marla Goldwasser, director of Affirmation Arts in New York, acknowledged her limited prior knowledge of Haitian art before organizing the 'Saving Grace' exhibit. The gallery aimed to contribute to Haiti's recovery by giving Haitian art and the Haitian people a voice through 'Saving Grace,' the first such show of Haitian art in the United States in over a decade. Many of the pieces had never been exhibited outside Haiti. Nader hopes viewers will appreciate the vital role art plays in Haitian society and understand the imperative to recover what the earthquake buried.
translated_content: Yvyryrýi guasu rire Haitípe, Georges Nader oipe'a porã Hector Hyppolite rembiapokue ita ári guare, peteĩ túva ohechakuaaháicha imemby ojerido ramo guáicha, hasẽsyry pukukue javeve. 'Vase et Fleurs,' peteĩ tembiapo porã arte naif rehegua, oñemopẽmba peteĩ rompecabezas komplikádoicha. Henda ambuépe ikuarahy'ã, ha ambue katu ndaipóri voi. Heta mba'e ojehu haguéicha Haitípe, pe ta'anga ojapova'ekue peteĩ umi artista tenondegua tetãmegua, okañy, peteĩ tembiapo guasu oho, ogueraha hendive peteĩ pehẽngue Haití rembiasakuégui. Nader, ohekýivo itakuéra apytépe peteĩ museo oñembyaíva Port-au-Prince-pe, oguereko va'ekue ifamília colección orekóva 12.000 tembiapokue, oguerovia avave ndaikatumo'ãiha ombojoaju jey. Peteĩteĩva omombe'u tembiasakue ha aspiraciones peteĩ tavaygua ohasava'ekue heta mba'e ha ojehechauka ta'anga ha escultura rupive. Ndaorekóivo umi institución establecidáva, edificios, ha monumentos tetãnguéra imba'ehetavéva oguerekóva, Haití oipuru umi ta'anga ojapóva kuarahy, yguasu, tekovekuéra, ha mymbakuéra rehegua umi artista ndoarandúiva—ambue katu omoinge tradiciones espirituales cultura voodoo-gui—ikatu haguãicha oiko chugui imandu'arã colectiva. Hyppolite, peteĩ pa'i voodoo ha artista oñemoarandúva ha'eño, oipuru ipo ha pinceles ojejapóva ryguasú rendágui opinta haguã. Ko arapýpe, Nader oñembo'ýta jey Hyppolite rembiapokue 1946-pe guare renondépe, ipy'aguapy rehegua, iporãitéva color-kuéra oñemoingove jey conservadores rupive oñomoirũva Smithsonian Institution ndive. Nader ohechauka ityre'ỹha, he'ívo ha'eha peteĩ 'milagro'. Pe ta'anga ha'e peteĩ umi mokõi tembiapo oñemyatyrõva oĩva peteĩ exhibición tuichavévape orekóva 50 tembiapokue artista Haitípegua ojapova'ekue. Ambue tembiapo ojesalvava'ekue ha'e 'Beau Reve' Celestin Faustin ojapova'ekue. 'Saving Grace: A Celebration of Haitian Art,' oorganisáva Affirmation Arts ha oisãmbyhýva karai arandu tembiapokue Haitípegua hérava Gerald Alexis, oreko peteĩ importancia tuichaitéva Alexis ha Nader-pe guarã. Oiko peteĩ símboloicha Haití renacimiento-gui, ko'ýte umi oje'évo mbeguekue ojejapo jey haguã umi mba'e yvyryrýi rire. Alexis ohechauka kóva ohechauka identidad tavaygua Haitípegua. He'i ojehejáramo kóva, umi generación oúva Haitípe ndoikuaamo'ãi moõguipa ou. Ha'e peteĩ tembiapo oreko va'erãva hikuái. Yvyryrýi oiko rire, Nader ha ambue umi oñongatúva tembiapokue Haitípegua osalva miles tembiapokue itakuéra apytégui, ojoko haguã ojeperdépama. Peteĩ kotýpe imuseope, osalva 1.000 tembiapokue, 70 por ciento oikotevẽva oñemyatyrõ. Ojeha'ãrõ va'erã mboy tembiapokue okañy, Nader he'i, ndaipórigui Haitípe hetaiterei museo ha galería Estados Unidos-pe oĩháicha. Heta mba'e porã oguereko tetã oĩ óga particular-pe ha umi colección privada-pe, itúva oguereko haguéicha, oñepyrũva oñongatu heta ary ohasava'ekuépe. Ndaipóri oikuaáva porã mboy tembiapokue okañy. Segundo piso igalería pegua oiko jave peteĩ tasyóicha tembiapokuépe guarã, Nader ojerreklama omoporã jeytaha opaite. Ha'e ha Alexis oñepyrũ ohenói umi experto-pe, oheka haguã umi ikatúva omoporã porã umi tembiapo. Oñomoirũ Smithsonian ndive, upéicha ojejapo Centro de Recuperación Cultural oñomoirũme gobierno Haití pegua ndive yvyty pa'ũme Port-au-Prince-pe. Patrimonio cultural Haití pegua, león Africagua oikóva guýicha, oĩ peligroguýpe. Pe centro rembiaporã ha'e oñangareko haguã upe patrimonio rehe. Richard Kurin, subsecretario tembiasakue, arte ha cultura rehegua Smithsonian-pe, he'i ndovaléiha ojeheja rei umi tembiapo itakuéra guýpe. He'i pe centro de recuperación 'mágicamente' omoporã jeyha miles tembiapokue oñembyaíva'ekue ha avei ombo'e umi Haitípe guare oñongatu haguã. Peteĩ curso jasyporundy jave ombo'e 26 participante-pe oikuaa haguã mba'épa ombyaí tembiapokuépe, mba'éichapa oñepyrũ oñangareko, mba'éichapa oñembosako'i umi emergencia-pe guarã ha mba'éichapa ojejapo umi tenda isegúrova oñongatu haguã umi colección. Kurin ohecha pe tembiapo jerekuperación ha'eha esperanza jerekuperación, ome'ẽvo tavayguakuérape oike haguã ipatrimonio-pe omoporã jeyvo yma guare. Marla Goldwasser, directora Affirmation Arts Nueva York-pe, ohechakuaa ndoikuaaiha heta mba'e arte Haití rehegua oorganisa mboyve exhibición 'Saving Grace'. Pe galería oipytyvõse jerekuperación Haití pegua ome'ẽvo arte Haití pegua ha tavaygua Haití pegua-pe peteĩ ñe'ẽ 'Saving Grace' rupive, kóva ha'e peteĩ exhibición arte Haití rehegua Estados Unidos-pe heta ary rire. Heta umi tembiapo ndojehechaukái gueteri okápe Haití-gui. Nader oipota umi ovy'áva pe tembiapo porã rehe oguereko peteĩ kuaapy mba'eichaitépa importante arte sociedad Haitípe ha ontende tekotevẽha ojejerekupera opa mba'e yvyryrýi oguereva'ekue jasyporãme.

article_content: Lara Clarke, a young baker with two years of experience, has created a sweet cake tribute to the Duchess of Cambridge. This unusual memento commemorates Kate's pregnancy. The Duchess is not the only celebrity transformed into sponge and icing; Clarke also creates edible figures of Johnny Depp, Yoda, and the Grinch. These handcrafted models take hours of intensive labor to achieve their realistic effect. The 27-year-old from Walsall, West Midlands, has created approximately 50 custom cakes in various shapes and sizes. Clarke said, 'When Kate Middleton announced her pregnancy, I created a white chocolate topper of the Duchess in celebration.' 'I wanted to show that I could make anybody out of chocolate, and she's so pretty it was a lovely challenge.' Among her tasty cake creations are Yoda and Toy Story's Buzz Lightyear. Clarke, who works for Tombola online bingo, hand-paints the figures with food coloring. The four-foot-high Grinch cake took over 40 hours to create and has an internal wooden structure to keep it upright. She explained, 'It was made of chocolate sponge and vanilla icing, covered in fondant.' 'There was enough to feed 500 people.' 'I taught myself to bake cakes from YouTube and TV shows. Once I started I just couldn't stop.' Clarke spends hours perfecting her realistic designs, such as a Triumph motorbike cake. Unusual customer requests include a beer can cake and a dog's head cake. One labor-intensive design features handbags, a rabbit, keys, euro notes, and a camera with a real photograph. Clarke's talent has led her business, Tasty Cakes, to receive requests for unique and crazy cakes. She stated, 'I get quite a lot of crazy cake requests, mostly for birthdays or weddings.' 'I once made a full dog head cake for a woman who wanted to celebrate her dog's birthday.' 'I love baking; the moment I start, I lose track of time and concentrate on making the cakes as life-like as possible.'

article_content: According to government data, the average retail price of onions across India was high at Rs 59.09 per kg on Monday. To curb the price increase, the central government imposed a minimum export price of USD 800 per tonne late last month to limit exports and increase the domestic supply. Retail prices had surged to approximately Rs 80 per kg due to limited supply. Data from the Consumer Affairs Ministry indicates that the all-India average price of onions on Monday was Rs 59.09 per kg. The highest recorded price was Rs 90 per kg, while the lowest was Rs 20 per kg. The all-India modal price stood at Rs 60 per kg. In Delhi, onion prices have decreased to Rs 60 per kg. Onion prices in the national capital began to gradually increase from October 25, when they were at Rs 40 per kg. Rates doubled to Rs 80 per kg by October 29. Onions are cultivated in three seasons: kharif, late kharif, and rabi. Only rabi onions are stored due to their longer shelf life. On October 28, the government implemented a minimum export price (MEP) of USD 800 per tonne on onion exports until December 31 of this year to enhance the availability of onions in the domestic market and moderate prices. This decision took effect on October 29. The USD 800 per tonne MEP is equivalent to about Rs 67 per kg. Furthermore, the government has announced the procurement of an additional 2 lakh tonnes of onions for the buffer stock, in addition to the 5 lakh tonnes already procured. The MEP applies to all onion varieties except Bangalore Rose and Krishnapuram onions, as well as those that are cut, sliced, broken, or in powder form. The government stated that this measure will help ensure sufficient onion availability for domestic consumers at reasonable prices, as the quantity of stored Rabi 2023 onions is decreasing. The country has exported approximately 15 lakh tonnes of onions up to October 20 of this fiscal year. Total onion exports amounted to 25 lakh tonnes in 2022-23, according to official data. The all-India average price of potatoes on Monday is Rs 25.24 per kg, while the average price of tomatoes is Rs 38.18 per kg. article_content: Rosa Bouglione, the celebrated matriarch of Paris' Winter Circus, became famous after marrying businessman Joseph Bouglione in 1928—inside a lion's cage. Now 103, she's lived decades past her husband's passing, yet still smiles when recalling her extraordinary life. At her Paris apartment entrance, Rosa, adorned with sparkling diamonds and red lipstick, uses a walking frame before settling beside her leopard skin rug. Pictured last month, Rosa Bouglione shows an art piece of her and her husband during their circus days. The artwork depicts their wedding day in 1928, held inside a lion's cage, and is displayed in her Paris apartment. Pointing to what's left of her former pet, she exclaims, 'That's Mickey. He passed away from old age. We had him for a very long time,' she says fondly, offering a Swiss chocolate to her visitor. Soon, stories pour out: marrying in a lion's den, bringing a baby primate in a hat box to a fancy hotel, and helping to raise a parrot known for its colorful French vocabulary. Madame Rosa is now seen as the circus's most unique, and oldest, character. Born Rosa Van Been in Belgium to a performing family just before Christmas in 1910, she found fame in Paris by marrying Bouglione, who bought the Winter Circus in 1934. Now she's a French celebrity. Pictures displayed in her apartment show glimpses of her life. Rosa was also close with Josephine Baker, the American-French dancer, singer, and actress. She also knew opera star Maria Callas and actresses Ingrid Bergman and Rita Hayworth—and outlived them all. With 54 grandchildren and great-grandchildren, Rosa has lived through two world wars and the Nazi occupation. However, the Winter Circus matriarch never let these trials ruin her joy for life. She chose a lions' cage for her wedding instead of a church. She recalls advising the pastor not to enter because of the animals. Her elephant respected the marriage, once pushing Callas for getting too close to her husband after a show. 'The elephant practically knocked her over... He was jealous,' Rosa said, laughing. Laughter is her lifeline; these often-told stories still bring light to her face when she remembers an image. She brought her 80-year-old son Emilien as a 'memory aid'. Once she begins, tales flow. There was her gorilla, Jackie, whom she brought to a hotel in a hat box. A footman joked about the hat's weight. For a month, nobody noticed the gorilla. Jackie also enjoyed wine. The parrot, Coco, also had a big personality, often swearing at Rosa. 'I cannot tell you what he would call me... They are very, very intelligent. He could speak very fluently,' she mentioned. Though her tales seem wild, photos and her son verify them. During her sea trip to Latin America in the 50's, a storm almost caused the captain to throw the elephants overboard. Emilien called it a 'miracle' when the storm suddenly stopped. 'That was an adventure,' says Madame Rosa. There were many celebrities too. Her son remembers stars like Bergman and Hayworth visiting the circus beneath the Eiffel Tower. Rosa met Callas and knew Baker well, sharing costume ideas with her. She gets sad when remembering those from her stories. 'They're all dead... They're all dead,' Rosa repeats, looking at her late husband's portrait. But with her family of performers in the annual Winter Circus, she doesn't dwell on the past. She says the secrets to her youthfulness are hard work, less sleep, and wild animals. 'I've always been with lions, with panthers, with wolves, with hyenas,' she says. 'I was never scared.' Finally, Rosa shares another secret: 'Fries,' she said. 'I'm Belgian.'
