Ko’áğa orekóma 103 ary, hetaiterei aryma ohasa iména omano rire, ha upéicharõ jepe opukavy gueteri imandu’ávo hekove iñambuévape. Hogarãme oikehápe París-pe, Rosa, ojehecharamóva diamante ha pintalabio pytãme, oipuru peteĩ yvyra oipytyvõva oguata hag̃ua oguahẽ mboyve iguapyhápe oĩháme peteĩ py pire jagua overáva. Oikuaa avei estrella de ópera Maria Callas ha umi kuñakarai oha’ãva Ingrid Bergman ha Rita Hayworth—ha ohasa hesekuéra opa. Oreko 54 temiarirõ ha rembinieta, Rosa ohasa mokõi guerra mundial ha pe ocupación nazi. Upéicharõ jepe, kuñakarai Winter Circus-pegua ndohejái ko’ã mba’e vai ombyai vy’a hekovére. Oiporavo jagua guasu koty omenda hag̃ua tupaópe rangue. Imandu’a he’írõguare upe pa’ípe ani oike umi mymba rehe. Imba’ejára guasu omomba’e upe ñemenda, peteĩ jevy omongu’i Callas-pe oñemoaĝuíre iména rehe peteĩ tembiapo rire. 'Upe elefánte reíma omongu’i chupe… Ipochy kuri,’ he’i Rosa opukávape. Pukavy ha’e hekove, umi mombe’upy oñemombe’úva py’ỹive ombojeguaka gueteri hesape imandu’árõ peteĩ ta’angáre. Ogueru imemby kuimba’e oguerekóva 80 ary Emilien ramo ‘oipytyvõ hag̃ua imandu’ápe’. Oñepyrũvo, osẽ mombe’upy. Oĩ va’ekue imbarakaja, Jackie, oguerúva peteĩ hotel-pe peteĩ mba’yru hatĩme. Peteĩ karai opuka hatĩ pohýire. Peteĩ jasy pukukue, avave ndohechakuaái upe mbarakaja. Jackie ovy’a avei víno rehe. Upe gua’a, Coco, oguereko avei peteĩ tekove guasu, py’ỹive he’íva ñe’ẽ ky’a Rosa-pe. ‘Ndaikatúi ha’e mba’épa he’íva chéve… Ha’ekuéra iñarandu eterei. Ikatúkuri oñe’ẽ porã,’ he’i. Jepe umi mombe’upy ipochy, ta’anga ha imemby ohechauka añeteha. Ohasárõguare para rupi Latinoamérica-pe umi 50 ary jave, peteĩ torménta omomýi haimete upe capitán omombo hag̃ua yguasúpe umi elefantekuéra. Emilien he’i ‘milagro’ ramo guare oguahẽvo pya’e upe torménta. ‘Upe niko peteĩ mba’e guasu,’ he’i Madame Rosa. Heta ava herakuãguáva oĩ avei. Imemby imandu’a umi estrella-kuéra Bergman ha Hayworth ovisitárõguare circo Eiffel ykére. Rosa oikuaa Callas ha oĩporã Baker ndive, omboja’óva hendive umi ao. Oñembyasy imandu’árõ umi mombe’upýre. ‘Opa omanóma… Opa omanóma,’ Rosa he’i jeyma omañávo iména ra’angáre. Ha katu hogayguakuéra oha’ãva reheve upe Winter Circus-pe, ndopytái imandu’ápe. He’i mba’épa ojapo itujami hag̃ua ha’e omba’apo hatã, oke mbovy ha oĩ mymba saite ndive. ‘Che aĩmantéma jagua guasu, jaguarete, aguara, mborevi ndive,’ he’i. ‘Nda kyhyjéi va’ekue araka’eve.’ Ipahápe, Rosa omombe’u mba’épa ojapo itujami hag̃ua: ‘Papa,’ he’i. ‘Che ha’e belga.’

article_content: A university student, Sophie Piggott, has been recognized with two awards for her profoundly moving documentary. The film chronicles the devastating loss of her mother and two brothers, who tragically died after being struck by a car while crossing a road. Sophie Piggott, now 20 and from Shrewsbury, Shropshire, captured her father's journey as a single parent following the tragedy. Her work has earned her the Best Documentary Short prize at both the Suffolk Film Festival and the Screen Stockport Film Festival. Her mother, Sarah Piggott, 42 and pregnant, her seven-year-old son Simon, who was seven years old, and her unborn child Sullivan, all perished in 2006 when a car hit them at 50 mph. The film, titled '26' in reference to the day of the tragedy, serves as a poignant tribute and features interviews with Sophie's father, Steve, who reflects on his 22-year marriage while watching footage from their wedding. Sam and Scott also share fond memories of their mom and brother. Christopher Ballantyne, the pub landlord responsible for the accident, was convicted of causing death by careless driving. He received a driving ban for 12 months and was ordered to pay £1,000 in costs. The heartrending incident occurred near the family home on June 26, 2006, leaving Steve to raise their other children: Sophie, who was 13, Sam, 16, and Scott, 10. Steve recounts the painful experience of holding his stillborn son, Sullivan, after the delivery. He shared that they allowed him to hold and see Sullivan, and you would think he was just sleeping. He also explained that Simon was instantly killed and Sarah was badly injured when they were crossing the street. The funeral of Sarah Piggott, her son Simon, and her unborn son took place on July 6, 2006, at St. Peters Church in Shrewsbury. Sophie, currently a third-year Media Film Production student at Staffordshire University, created the film to honor her family's memory. She said she wanted to wait until she was ready, it was difficult to do. She added that her classmates were shocked when they saw the film, as they didn't know about this part of her life. Editing her dad's interview was particularly emotional for her. Despite the pain, Sophie believes that time helps to heal and that making documentaries is her passion. Her father is proud of her work, and she believes her mother would have been too. The documentary incorporates clips from Sullivan's ultrasound scan, adding another layer of emotional depth to the story. Steve expresses his initial reluctance to watch the completed film but is now grateful that he did, praising Sophie's sensitive approach. The entire family finds the film to be a beautiful way to remember the happy times. Steve remarked that the experience has taught him not to procrastinate and to pursue one's dreams. Floral tributes were left at the site of the accident on Robertson Way in Shrewsbury.

Omombe'u avei Simon omano hague upepete ha Sarah ojeherido vaiete kuri ohasávo hikuái tape. Sarah Piggott, imemby Simon ha imemby'ỹre oñeñotỹ 6 jasypokõi 2006-pe, St. Peters tupão Shrewsbury-pe. Sophie, ko'ág̃a oestudia mbohapyha ary Cine ha Medios de Comunicación Universidad de Staffordshire-pe, ojapo upe película omomba'eguasu haguã ifamília. He'i oha'arõ hague oĩ porã meve, hasy hague ojapo haguã. Omombe'u avei ikompañerokuéra oñesorprende hague ohechávo pe película, ndoikuaágui hikuái upe mba'e ohasava'ekue. Omohenda rire itúva entrevista, oñeñandu vaieterei. Hasy ramo jepe, Sophie oguerovia ára oipytyvõha oñemyatyrõ haguã ha ojapo haĝua película ha'eha hembiapo porãvéva. Itúva ovy'aiterei hembiapóre, ha oguerovia isy avei ovy'aitereitaha. Pe película oreko ra'anga Sullivan ecografía-gui, ombojoapýva mba'e hypy'ũve upe istóriape. Steve he'i iñepyrũrã ndohechaseiete hague pe película opa rire, ha katu ko'ág̃a oagradece ojapo haguére, omomba'eguasúvo mba'éichapa Sophie ohechauka porã upe mba'e. Opaite ifamíliape guarã, ko película ha'e peteĩ tape iporãva imandu'a haguã umi ára porãre. Steve he'i upe mba'e ohasava'ekue ombo'e chupe ani haguã omboyke mba'eve ko'ẽrõ guarã ha oha'arõ haguã isueño-kuéra. article_content: Scott Tinsley has been sentenced to 40 months in jail after he was discovered sleeping on a sofa in the home he was burglarizing. The burglar, Scott Tinsley, was found asleep on a sofa inside a Stoke-on-Trent home he was attempting to steal from. Tinsley was found snoring on the settee after breaking into the house in the early hours. The Stoke-on-Trent Crown Court heard the 38-year-old from Cobridge, Staffordshire, had already moved electrical goods from the house into the garden. He then went back inside the house to find something to eat and drink but fell asleep on the sofa after taking drugs, also leaving the gas turned on. Tinsley was discovered at 7:30 a.m. the next morning asleep in the front room. The court was told the burglary, which occurred last November, was supposed to be a quick way to get money by selling electrical goods. The mother living at the house called the police after finding him snoring in the living room. Prosecutor Neil Ahuja said she was particularly concerned because her three children were asleep upstairs. She and her husband woke Tinsley, who tried to leave but was detained. Various valuables, including the television, games console, and CD player, had been moved from the front room outside and were found by police in a back garden two doors down. The court also heard that Tinsley's relationship had ended, and he had returned to drug use. Defense lawyer Simon Leech said Tinsley did not respond with violence and acknowledged the incident would have been frightening for the family and dangerous if the gas had ignited. Tinsley pleaded guilty to burglary at a hearing at Stoke-on-Trent Crown Court. Judge Nigel Daly sentenced him to 40 months in jail, calling him the most 'pathetic' burglar in history. Judge Daly noted Tinsley had 102 offences from 41 convictions and said he was 'so off your head' that he fell asleep during the burglary and that he was 'a rather pathetic figure'. He added, 'This was a domestic burglary with people in the home, including young children, and it took place at night. In your drugged-up state you managed to leave the gas on and helped yourself to food as well as valuable goods. The trauma of finding that must have been considerable for the parents.'
translated_content: Ojeapresa Scott Tinsley-pe 40 meses cárcelpe ojuhúgui hikuái oke peteĩ sofápe peteĩ ógape, oikehaguépe omonda hag̃ua. Pe mondaha, Scott Tinsley, ojejuhu oke peteĩ sofápe peteĩ ógape Stoke-on-Trent-pe, oñeha'ãrõguare omonda. Tinsley ojejuhu ipópe ojepyku'ígui haguépe oike rire ógape pyhareve jave. Pe Tribunal de la Corona Stoke-on-Trent-pe ohendu pe karai 38 ary orekóva Cobridge, Staffordshire-gua, ombohasáma kuri umi mba'e elétrico óga guive hardínpe. Upéi oike jey ógape oheka hag̃ua mba'e ho'u ha hoy'u hag̃ua, ha ho'a oke sofápe odroga rire, avei oheja pe gas ojeke. Tinsley ojejuhu 7:30 a.m. ko'ẽtĩme oke koty renondépe. Tribunal-pe oje'e pe mondaha oikova'ekue jasypateĩme, ojejapóne kuri pya'e ojehupyty hag̃ua pirapire ohepyme'ẽvo umi mba'e elétrico. Pe sy oikóva upe ógape ohenói policía-pe ojuhu rire chupe ipópe koty guasúpe. Fiscal Neil Ahuja he'i oipy'apyeterei chupe mbohapy mitã oke haguére yvate gotyo. Ha'e ha iména omombáy Tinsley-pe, oha'ãva osẽ, ha katu ojejokova'ekue chupe. Heta mba'e hepýva, umíva apytépe televisión, consola de juegos ha CD player, oñembohasa kuri koty renondégui okápe ha ojejuhu policía-kuéra peteĩ hardínpe mokõi óga mombyry. Tribunal-pe ojehendu avei Tinsley rehenói opa hague ha ojevy jey oipuru hag̃ua droga. Abogado de defensa Simon Leech he'i Tinsley nombohovái hague violencia reheve ha ohechakuaa pe oikova'ekue omongyhyjéne hague familia-pe ha ipeligrosoiterei kuri gas ojeke ramo. Tinsley oñe'ẽkuaa culpable oikérõguare omonda peteĩ audiencia-pe Tribunal de la Corona Stoke-on-Trent-pe. Juez Nigel Daly ome'ẽ chupe 40 meses cárcelpe, he'ívo ha'eha pe mondaha 'ipatético' véva historia-pe. Juez Daly ohechakuaa Tinsley oreko hague 102 delito 41 condena-gui ha he'i 'itavyeterei' hague ho'a haguépe oke omonda aja ha ha'eha 'peteĩ tapicha ipatéticoitereíva'. He'ive, 'Kóva ha'e kuri peteĩ mondaha doméstica ogapýpe oĩva, umíva apytépe mitãrusu, ha oiko pyhare. Nde estado de droga-pe ikatúkuri reheja pe gas ojeke ha reipytyvõ ndejehe ho'u hag̃ua ha avei mba'e hepýva. Pe trauma ojejuhúvo upéva tuichaiterei va'erã umi tuvakuérape.'

article_content: By Sean Poulter, Consumer Affairs Editor PUBLISHED: 12:19 EST, September 5, 2013 | UPDATED: 07:24 EST, September 16, 2013 Humble pie was the dish of the day at Waitrose yesterday – and Delia Smith must surely have been first in the queue to see it served. Months after the Queen of TV cookery stopped appearing in TV advertisements and Pippa Middleton was hired as a magazine columnist, the supermarket has decided to reinstate her. In a U-turn, the grocery giant has asked the much-loved cook to bring her successful online culinary school to its website. Triumphant return: Delia Smith has been signed up again by Waitrose. The supermarket's customers were annoyed when Pippa Middleton was given a column in the store magazine soon after Delia departed. The move follows anger in the kitchens of Middle Britain over Waitrose’s decision to drop her from its television ad campaign last year, while promoting Miss Middleton. Customers saw the decision as a betrayal of a woman who had taught two generations to cook, and the resulting Twitter storm suggested it was a ‘gratuitous insult’ to customers, with some threatening a supermarket boycott. Her departure was followed by the news that Waitrose had hired the Duchess of Cambridge’s sister as the new star columnist for its magazine. The news irked many Delia lovers, not least because the 29-year-old’s culinary experience seemed limited to enjoying hospitality at celebrity parties and making sushi rolls for her university friends. Added to that was the widespread mocking of her Celebrate party planning book, which had disastrous sales. Pippa was signed as a columnist for Waitrose's monthly magazine, Waitrose Kitchen. Yesterday, enthusiastic bosses at Waitrose announced their ‘exciting new move’ to work with Delia again. Her online cookery school, launched earlier this year, will appear on the Waitrose TV section of the supermarket’s website, offering a free video library of lessons and techniques from beginner to advanced level. Waitrose chiefs were positively effervescent yesterday, calling Delia’s tutorials the ‘hero of the channel’ and praising her ‘inspiration and expertise’. Waitrose marketing director Rupert Thomas said: ‘We have a long and successful history of working with Delia, and we’re thrilled to be joining forces again on the Delia Online Cookery School with Waitrose, which we believe will be the definitive online tool for cookery tuition.’ Delia, who has sold 21 million cookery books, maintained her dignity throughout the controversy. When it was suggested she might want to prepare one of Pippa’s recipes at home, she simply laughed. Yesterday, the 72-year-old spoke of her ‘ambition’ to teach anyone who wants to learn to cook. ‘If you are from nine to 109, you will be able to learn anything from boiling an egg to baking a cake – I don’t think you can learn in a better way,’ she said. Icon: Delia has been a popular mainstay of the British culinary scene for decades.

article_content: Even bundled in a purple jacket and light blue turtleneck sweater, and warming herself in a thick canvas emergency tent heated by a stove, the young Ukrainian woman still feels the bitter chill. 'It is very cold,' she said. 'The frost is very strong. It's very slippery out there.' She is among the fortunate ones, finding refuge from the harsh winter in eastern Europe within a temporary shelter provided by the Ukrainian government. 'Here it's warm, and there's food and drink,' she stated. Another man taking shelter added, 'It's very important, especially for people like us in this unfortunate situation.' Across the region, at least 250 people have died during this cold spell, with 135 of those deaths occurring in Ukraine. Ukrainian authorities have established an emergency hospital to treat those suffering from cold-related illnesses and have distributed 3,000 emergency relief tents nationwide. These heated tents offer hot food and drinks to those with nowhere else to go. Kiev has over 14,000 homeless individuals, according to authorities, making them particularly vulnerable to the winter conditions. Since January 27, approximately 2,000 people have been hospitalized due to the cold, officials reported. Ukrainian energy minister Yuri Boyko noted that electricity consumption in the country is at record highs. In Bosnia, state news agency FENA reported that two men on snowmobiles finally reached the isolated village of Zijemlja, which had been cut off for five days. Residents in some areas of Bosnia were warned about the potential for avalanches. FENA also reported that the inhabitants of the Sarajevo Zoo were in winter quarters and had sufficient food. Polish TVN reported that more than 50 people, mostly homeless, have died in Poland in recent weeks. The Russian government reported at least 64 deaths due to the cold in Russia. Snow has fallen as far west as Spain and caused traffic delays in Brussels, Belgium. In southeastern Europe, near the Mediterranean Sea, snowfall is blocking roads and isolating communities, hindering access to essential supplies. Meteorologists predict more heavy snow for southeastern Europe, while the northeast is expected to experience temperatures significantly below average. Cold air from Siberia is interacting with maritime moisture from the Mediterranean Sea, resulting in frozen precipitation. This pattern is expected to continue, with Bosnia, Serbia, and Macedonia anticipating further snowfall. The extreme cold in the northeast has proven more deadly than the snow farther south, with many succumbing to hypothermia. In Romania, where at least 39 people have died due to the cold snap, all 'national roads' (two-lane highways) in seven southern and eastern counties were completely blocked, according to state news agency Agerpres on Monday. Traffic in the capital, Bucharest, was chaotic, and blizzards were forecast for half the country in the coming days. In Italy, the Italian ANSA news agency reported that a Milan court delayed the trial of former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi on bribery charges on Monday due to the low temperatures in the courtroom. The trial was moved to warmer chambers, often used for another case involving Berlusconi, where he faced accusations of paying for sex with a minor – a Moroccan girl known as 'Ruby.' Meteorologists forecast that the severe cold will persist throughout the week.

article_content: In San Francisco, drag performers are in conflict with Facebook due to its mandate that individuals utilize their legal names, instead of performance names like Pollo Del Mar and Heklina. The social network maintains its stance on this rule. Recently, Facebook has been removing profiles belonging to drag performers and others who use stage names. This action stems from their non-compliance with the platform's requirement that users identify themselves by their ‘real names’. Following a meeting involving drag performers and a San Francisco supervisor, Facebook announced on Wednesday that it would not revise its policy. The company states it typically deletes accounts with fictitious names after investigating user-submitted complaints. During a press conference held at San Francisco City Hall, Supervisor David Campos, supported by several drag performers, voiced his opposition to Facebook's policy, calling it ‘wrong and misguided.’ Drag performers, along with members of the LGBTQ+ community, argue that many Facebook users fear using their actual names for various reasons, including potential threats to their safety and job security. Heklina, a drag performer, explained her reluctance by stating she has family members she prefers not to contact her through Facebook. Facebook has temporarily reinstated hundreds of deleted accounts for a two-week period. Afterward, users must either change their name to their legal name or convert their profile into a fan page. Sister Roma, of the Sisters of Perpetual Indulgence, commented that numerous individuals have valid reasons to use pseudonyms. Campos and the drag performers are planning another meeting with Facebook, hoping to persuade the company to reconsider its policy. If Facebook refuses to change its policy, the drag performers have threatened to organize protests and boycotts. Facebook defends its policy by stating that it ‘helps prevent bad behavior, while creating a safer and more accountable environment.’ The company suggests that performers can use alternative methods, like business or public figure pages, to maintain their stage identities. Performers argue that fan pages are not equivalent to regular Facebook pages, limiting their audience reach. Rosa Sifuentes, also known as Bunny Pistol, emphasized this limitation. Facebook's 'real name' policy has been in place for nearly as long as the platform itself. It has faced criticism in the past, particularly from political activists who risk danger if their identities are exposed. In 2011, Chinese blogger Michael Anti, known legally as Zhao Jing, had his profile removed for using his professional name, despite its long-standing recognition. Lady Gaga, whose legal name is Stefani Joanne Angelina Germanotta, has seemingly reached a compromise by merging her stage name with her legal name on Facebook. Identifying authentic names can be challenging, leading to the deletion of accounts belonging to individuals with real names that appear fictitious. Facebook asserts its 'real names' policy is designed to foster accountability, reduce online negativity and bullying. Furthermore, real names facilitate targeted advertising to its vast user base of 1.32 billion. Facebook estimates that 6 to 11 percent of its monthly user accounts were either duplicate or fake in 2013. While the company acknowledges that estimates are lower in developed markets, and higher in developing markets, they are also based on internal review of a limited sample of accounts. The company uses significant judgement in this determination.

Pe compañía ohechauka umi artista ikatuhague ojepuru ambue método, página empresarial ha umi figura pública-pe guarãicha, oñemantene haguã héra escenario-pe. Facebook rembiaporã ‘héra tee’ rehegua oguereko ojeguereko haguãicha plataforma voi. Ohasáma rupi oñe’ẽ vai hese, ikatúramo umi activista político arriesga ikatúramo ojehechauka héra tee. Ary 2011-pe, blogger chino Michael Anti, ojekuaáva legalmente Zhao Jing ramo, oñemboja’o iprofil ojepuru haguére héra profesional, jepémo are guivéma ojekuaa. Lady Gaga, héra tee Stefani Joanne Angelina Germanotta, ojapo peteĩ acuerdo ombojoajúvo héra escenario-pe héra legal Facebook-pe. Ojehechakuaa héra añeteguáva ikatu hasy, upévare ojeipe’a umi cuenta oguerekóva héra tee ojoguáva gua’úvape. Facebook he’i ipolítica ‘héra tee’ rehegua ojejapoha oñemoheñói haguã responsabilidad, oñemboguejy haguã umi mba’e vai red-pe ha umi acoso. Avei, umi héra tee oipytyvõ publicidad ojegueraha porãve haguã ijepuruharakuérape, 1.32 billones. Facebook oguereko 6 térã 11 por ciento umi cuenta jepurúva peteĩ mes-pe ha’eha cuenta gua’u ary 2013-pe. Jepémo pe compañía he’i michĩveha umi estimaciones umi mercado desarrollado-pe, ha tuichave umi mercado en desarrollo-pe, oje’e avei ojejapo hague peteĩ análisis interno umi cuenta rehegua. article_content: Broadway enjoyed a financially robust Thanksgiving week, with a notable surge in box office earnings. For the week concluding on November 25, an impressive twelve shows on Broadway each exceeded $1 million in revenue, marking a first for the year according to the Broadway League. The frontrunners included well-known musical productions such as 'Wicked,' which grossed $2.3 million, 'The Lion King' with $2.1 million, and 'The Book of Mormon' bringing in $1.8 million. 'Spider-Man: Turn Off the Dark' also performed strongly with $1.78 million. The newly revived 'Annie' secured fifth place, achieving $1.5 million in ticket sales. This figure represents 105 percent of its potential earnings and set a new house record at the Palace Theatre. Ticket prices averaged $116 due to premium charges, up from $89 the previous week. Capitalizing on seasonal appeal, 'A Christmas Story: The Musical,' which debuted the previous Monday, generated $1.1 million during the week. An additional ninth show helped bolster its box office performance, reaching 70 percent of its potential gross. Another stage adaptation of a holiday film, 'Elf,' narrowly missed the million-dollar mark, earning $997,000 from eight shows, which is approximately 60 percent of its potential revenue. Completing the list of million-dollar earners were 'Once' ($1.17 million), 'The Phantom of the Opera' ($1.13 million), 'Mary Poppins' ($1.12 million), 'Newsies' ($1.11 million), 'Evita' ($1.01 million), and 'Jersey Boys' ($1.01 million). The Al Pacino-starring revival of 'Glengarry Glen Ross' had an unusual week, partially due to its official previews before its December 8 premiere. The show reduced its schedule to five performances over Thanksgiving, leading to a dip in earnings to $853,737, down from $1.16 million the week before. In contrast, 'Scandalous,' a biography musical of Aimee Semple McPherson with lyrics by Kathie Lee Gifford, faced challenges. Its first full week post-November 15 opening yielded only $194,511, less than 16 percent of its potential, with attendance at less than a third capacity. Its future seems uncertain.

Umi tenondete apytépe oĩ umi tembiapo herakuã guasueteháicha 'Wicked', ohupytyva’ekue 2,3 millones dólar, 'The Lion King' 2,1 millones ndive, ha 'The Book of Mormon' ogueruva 1,8 millones dólar. article_content: The Fox network is facing criticism for a controversial joke in the upcoming 'Simpsons' and 'Family Guy' crossover episode. The joke, which references rape, has led to calls for its removal. He believes such humor trivializes sexual assault. The scene involves Bart Simpson instructing Stewie Griffin on prank calls. Stewie then makes a call with a disturbing punchline. While RAINN's spokeswoman, Katherine Hull Fliflet, suggests the show may be highlighting that rape is not funny, others disagree. Seth MacFarlane, 'Family Guy' creator, expects criticism but defends the joke's context. This is not the first time 'Family Guy' has received backlash. Previous episodes have been criticized for content considered offensive to various groups, occasionally resulting in episodes being withheld.

article_content: Is a single finger test a reliable measure of beauty? A social media trend suggests it might be. On Weibo, the Chinese equivalent of Facebook, countless users are participating in the 'Beauty and Ugliness Identification Method,' also known as the 'finger trap test'. How does it work? Place your index finger against your chin and nose. If your lips touch the finger, you're considered 'beautiful'. Otherwise, the results suggest you are not considered traditionally beautiful. The 'finger trap test' is trending in over 200,000 Weibo discussions, even attracting participation from Chinese celebrities. This trend is considered China's digital version of 'Hot or Not'. It's loosely based on the 3.1 ratio theory used by cosmetic surgeons to achieve the 'perfect profile,' aligning the nose, lips, and chin in a straight line. Dr. Mark Holmes of McIndoe Surgical Centre notes that this test is related to facial symmetry and proportions, referencing Rickett's E-line. He clarifies, however, that while symmetry is a component of beauty, the test overlooks personality and energy. Consultant cosmetic surgeon Brent Tanner from Spire Tunbridge Wells Hospital and other institutions adds that the test, although rooted in classical principles dating back to Leonardo Da Vinci, oversimplifies beauty, which is influenced by diverse racial characteristics and cultural ideals. The concept originates from the 1950s work of orthodontist Dr. Robert Ricketts, who defined the 'E-plane' as a line from the nose tip to the chin tip. He believed that in a 'pleasing facial profile' of the average Caucasian face, the lips would touch this plane – or the finger in the 'finger trap test'.

article_content: As the Frankfurt Motor Show opens its doors, the world's leading car manufacturers are competing fiercely. The show features the latest hybrid and concept designs from prominent brands. While Frankfurt showcases this spectacle, manufacturers are focused on the growing car buyer base in China, over 6,000 miles away, where 200 million cars already navigate congested roads. China, the world's largest car market, is a key battleground for European companies in the 21st century, with premium brands aiming to tap into a population of 1.3 billion. With European sales declining and the U.S. market recovering slowly, China offers steady growth during economic uncertainty. High domestic demand and rising wages are driving growth in China, the world's second-largest economy, with car sales showing consistent gains. World Bank data indicates that China's GDP per capita rose 436% between 2002 and 2012, from $1,135 to $6,091. Consultancy PricewaterhouseCoopers reported in the past that by 2019, China's car market was projected to nearly equal the combined size of the U.S. and Western European markets, with sales expected to double. While this projection was made, current market conditions should be consulted for the most up-to-date information. Chinese motorists, once content with older domestic vehicles or imitations of Western designs like Mercedes-Benz and BMW, now prefer authentic Western brands, analysts say. Andrew Marsh of AutoIndustryInsider.com noted a similar trend with the rising middle class in India, stating that affluent consumers prefer Western brands over domestically produced goods. U.S. auto giants Ford and General Motors reported record sales increases in China for August of the past reporting period. Ford's sales rose significantly, driven by strong demand for the Focus, while GM's Buick sales increased notably compared to previous periods. McLaren Automotive also announced its entry into the Chinese market, opening showrooms in major cities to target China's expanding middle class. CEO Mike Flewitt stated that McLaren aims for China to contribute a significant portion of its total sales. McLaren's supercar range, including models like the 12C, 12C Spider, and P1, launched in China. The 12C and Spider were priced between £165,000 and £195,000, while the P1 cost approximately £866,000. James Foxall of the Daily Telegraph highlighted that foreign carmakers face challenges entering the Chinese market, including the requirement for joint ventures with local manufacturers. GM partners with Shanghai Automotive Industry Corporation (SAIC), while Ford has a three-way venture with Changan and Mazda. McLaren's Flewitt stated that the company is not overly concerned about counterfeiting, citing continuous investment in R&D. Paolo Beconcini of Carroll, Burdick and McDonough suggests that Chinese consumers prioritize design and status over technology and safety, viewing cars primarily as a status symbol.

article_content: The death of Lashano Gilbert, a medical school graduate from the Bahamas, while in police custody in New London, Connecticut, has been ruled a homicide. However, authorities state that this determination does not necessarily imply criminal actions by the involved officers. The Day newspaper reports that the chief medical examiner's office recently determined the October death of 31-year-old Lashano Gilbert to be a homicide. The cause was attributed to a physical altercation with police, which led to complications arising from a pre-existing sickle cell disease. According to police reports, Gilbert was initially arrested for an attempted carjacking. He died after resisting officers and being subjected to two stun gun deployments within an eight-hour period. The initial struggle occurred during the arrest, and a subsequent altercation took place at the police station after Gilbert allegedly attacked officers. State police are currently conducting an investigation into Gilbert's death. Gilbert reportedly told police that he was experiencing auditory hallucinations. When he allegedly behaved in a threatening manner, officers used a stun gun. Following the initial incident, Gilbert was taken to a hospital for treatment before being transported to the New London police station. Police state that while in a holding cell, Gilbert began manipulating his pants, seemingly attempting to fashion a noose. When officers opened the cell to confiscate the pants, Gilbert charged at them, resulting in a second tasering. He was then transported to the hospital again and pronounced dead around 3:30 a.m. on Saturday. New London's state's attorney and police chief promptly requested an investigation by the state police, as reported by NBC Connecticut. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) describes sickle cell disease as an inherited blood disorder that can obstruct blood flow and lead to pain and other serious complications, such as infection, acute chest syndrome, and stroke. Gilbert’s cousin, Kasi Fletcher, conveyed to The Day that the family is deeply affected by the news. 'It’s hard to hold back the emotions with something like this,' Fletcher stated. 'We’re all still pretty much in shock. We informed (Gilbert’s) mother, and she just wants justice.' Fletcher also indicated that the family has received minimal expressions of sympathy from town officials or the police department regarding Gilbert’s death. 'Not a word,' Fletcher said. 'Crickets.' The homicide ruling indicates that Gilbert's death was at least partly caused by the actions of another person. Gilbert's family reportedly learned of the ruling the previous week. Local police union President Todd Lynch stated on Friday that officers have faced criticism for simply performing their duties. 'There are situations that our officers must respond to,' Lynch said. 'We cannot run away or call for assistance. We have to act, regardless of color, creed, sexual orientation, religion, or anything else. That’s what our officers did that night.' 'None of the officers involved wanted to go home that night thinking their actions caused the death of someone. Nobody wants this to happen,' Lynch concluded.
translated_content: Lashano Gilbert, peteĩ mbo’ehao pohanohára Bahamagua guare, omano kuri policía kuéra poguýpe táva New London, Connecticut-pe, ha oje’e hembyreitére omanohague. Ha katu, mburuvichakuéra he’i ko mba’e ndaha’éi he’ise umi policía ojapo hague peteĩ mba’e vai. Kuatiahaipyre hérava The Day omombe’u mburuvicha pohanohára rendota he’i ramoitére pe octubre-pe omano hague Lashano Gilbert, orekóva 31 ary, ha omanohague. Oje’e omano hague oñorairõ haguére policía ndive, ha upéva ogueru kuri hasyve pe mba’asy oguerekóva hérava 'sickle cell'. Polícia kuéra kuatiápe he’i Gilbert-pe ojejagarra raẽ oha’ãre omonda peteĩ mba’yru. Omano kuri oñemoĩ rire policía kuérare ha ojeporu hese mokõi jey peteĩ mba’e ojeporuva oporombohasa asy hag̃ua ocho hora pukuépe. Pe ñorairõ guasu oiko kuri ojejagarrahápe chupe, ha upéi oiko jey ambue ñorairõ guasu estación de policía-pe Gilbert oataka rire angeái policía kuérare. Ko’ág̃a policía estatal oinvestiga hína Gilbert ñemano. Gilbert omombe’u kuri policía kuérape ohenduha mba’e, ha ojejapo vai angeái, policía kuéra ojeporu hese pe mba’e oporombohasa asýva. Upe oiko rire, Gilbert-pe ojegueraha peteĩ tasyópe oñepohano hag̃ua ha upéi ojegueraha estación de policía táva New London-pe. Polícia kuéra he’i Gilbert oĩ aja peteĩ koty’ípe, oñepyrũ kuri omongu’e ijao, ojaposéva guáicha chugui peteĩ laso. Policía kuéra oipe’ávo pe koty’i oguerahase hag̃ua chugui ijao, Gilbert oataka angeái chupekuéra, ha upévare ojeporu jey hese pe mba’e oporombohasa asýva. Upéi ojegueraha jey chupe tasyópe ha omano 3:30 a.m. rupi ág̃a sábado. Abogado estatal ha mburuvicha policía táva New London-gua ojerure voi policía estatal-pe oinvestiga hag̃ua ko mba’e, he’i NBC Connecticut. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) he’i pe mba’asy hérava 'sickle cell' ha’eha peteĩ mba’asy oúva tuguy rupive ikatúva omboty pe tuguy rape ha ogueru hasy ha ambue mba’e vai, techapyrã infección, mba’asy vaiete pecho-pe ha derrame cerebral. Gilbert primokue, Kasi Fletcher, omombe’u The Day-pe ifamilia oñeñandu vaieterei ko marandu rehe. 'Hasy jajoko hag̃ua ñande py’aro ko mba’e oikóvare,' he’i Fletcher. 'Roime gueteri ropytũ. Romombe’u (Gilbert) sýpe, ha ha’e oipota tojejapo tekojoja.' Fletcher he’i avei ifamilia ndohendúi gueteri mba’eveichagua ñembyasy mburuvichakuéra távagui térã departamento de policía-gui Gilbert ñemanóre. 'Ndaipóri peteĩ ñe’ẽ,' he’i Fletcher. 'Kirirĩ.' Pe ñe’ẽ he’íva omanohague he’ise Gilbert ñemano oikova’ekue ambue ava ojapo haguére. Gilbert familia oikuaa kuri pe mba’e oje’éva pe semana ohasava’ekuépe. Mburuvicha sindicato policía-gua hérava Todd Lynch he’i ág̃a viernes umi policía-pe ojejapahague hesekuéra mba’e vai ojapo haguére hembiapo. 'Oĩ situación ore policía kuéra oñembohovái va’erã,' he’i Lynch. 'Ndaikatúi roñani térã rohenói ambuépe oipytyvõ hag̃ua. Rojapo va’erã, taha’e ha’éva ipire kolór, ijerovia, mba’éichapa ojehecha kuimba’éramo térã kuñáramo, irreligión térã mba’eveichagua mba’e. Upéva ha’e ore policía kuéra ojapo va’ekue upe pyharépe.' 'Avave umi policía oĩva upépe ndohoséi hógape upe pyharépe opensávo hembiapo ojapova’ekue ojuka hague peteĩ tapichápe. Avave ndoipotái ko mba’e oiko,' he’i Lynch.

article_content: Virat Kohli's 50th century at Mumbai's Wankhede stadium in the World Cup semi-final sparked a biryani frenzy in Uttar Pradesh's Bahraich district, leading to a large gathering at a local eatery. The eatery owner offered a discount on biryani equal to the runs scored by Kohli. As Kohli reached his record-breaking 50th century, the discount reached 100%, making chicken and mutton biryani free for customers. This promotion quickly went viral, causing a surge of people to rush to the eatery. The incident occurred in the Tikoni Bagh area within the Dehat police jurisdiction on Wednesday evening. The offer attracted a large crowd, resulting in chaos as people jostled to get a plate of biryani. The restaurant quickly ran out of biryani, causing tension among those waiting. The owner chained the restaurant to prevent potential vandalism. Police were dispatched to maintain order. Virat Kohli surpassed Sachin Tendulkar's record of 49 one-day international centuries. Tendulkar congratulated Kohli, expressing happiness that an Indian broke his record.

article_content: Jerome Kerviel, implicated in France's largest rogue-trading incident, was unsuccessful in his appeal against his prison term on Wednesday. He was penalized for gambling â‚¬50 billion (approximately $65 billion) of a French bank's funds without consent. The Paris court affirmed the five-year sentence, with two years suspended, initially imposed in October 2010, stated Kerviel's legal representative, David Koubbi. This verdict requires Kerviel to serve three years of imprisonment. Additionally, the court upheld the demand for Kerviel to provide â‚¬4.9 billion (around $6.3 billion) in restitution to Societe Generale. Koubbi expressed outside the courthouse, as reported by CNN affiliate BFM-TV, 'We committed to defending Mr. Kerviel from what we believe is a severe injustice. We will continue to stand by him.' Koubbi mentioned that the legal team will deliberate on potentially appealing to France's highest court, the Cour de Cassation. Jean Veil, representing Societe Generale, told BFM-TV he felt 'great satisfaction with the court's decision to recognize Jerome Kerviel as solely accountable for the deception.' The bank welcomed the initial judgment because it assigned the blame for the unauthorized trades to Kerviel instead of the institution. If Kerviel's conviction was overturned, questions regarding the bank's involvement could resurface. The bank had hinted it might not pursue Kerviel for the damages, considering the amount unpayable even over many lifetimes. The former Societe Generale employee faced charges including forgery, breach of trust, and unauthorized computer usage during his June 2010 trial. The bank reported losses of almost $6 billion because of unhedged bets. Kerviel admitted to computer abuse, but his previous lawyer, Olivier Metzner, urged jurors to acquit his client of breach of trust and forgery. Metzner previously told CNN that the environment at Societe Generale significantly influenced Kerviel's actions. 'The banks, not Jerome Kerviel, should be blamed for the banking system and the recurring economic downturn,' he argued. Metzner filed the appeal, but Kerviel replaced him with Koubbi in March. Koubbi regretted that 'despite new evidence,' Kerviel's appeal failed. Kerviel traded European index futures for the bank. He claimed he acted with his superiors' knowledge and was the only one charged in the case. 'I am convinced that the file has enough evidence to show that my superiors knew and covered for me. At the very least, I shouldn't be the only one being judged,' he told CNN after his memoir release, 'Trapped in a Spiral: Memoirs of a Trader,' defending his innocence. 'These managers earned significant bonuses based on the growing profits I was generating for the bank,' he added. Societe Generale stated that supervisors were never aware of Kerviel's unlawful actions when the losses were discovered in January 2008. CNN's Dheepthi Namasivayam, Sybile Penhirin, and Pierre Meilhan contributed to this article.

Oñemoĩ chupe kastígo ojuegágui â‚¬50 mil millones (haimete $65 mil millones) peteĩ banco Francés pirapire rehe, ndojeikuaa'ỹre ichupe. Koubbi omyesakã tribunal renondépe, he'iháicha CNN afiliada BFM-TV, 'Ore roñekompromete rodefende haguã karai Kerviel peteĩ mba'e vai guasúgui. Roseguíta roipytyvõ ichupe.' Koubbi omombe'u abogado kuéra ohesa'ỹijotaha ikatúpa ojapo peteĩ apelación Corte de Casación Franciapeguápe. Jean Veil, oĩháicha Societe Generale rérape, omombe'u BFM-TVpe oñeñandu porãitereiha 'corte odesidi haguére Jerome Kerviel ha'eño oĩha responsable ko tembiapo vai apópe.' Banco oguerohory decisión oñepyrũguare porque ome'ẽ responsabilidad umi negocio vai apóre Kervielpe, ndaha'éi instituciónpe. Oñemboykéramo Kerviel je'ói, ikatúkuri ojejapojey porandu banco rembiapóre ko mba'évai guasúpe. Banco he'i kuri ndojekobrái va'erã Kervielpe indemnización, ojehechakuaágui ndopagamo'ãiha jepe hekovépe. Umi ex-empleado Societe Generale pegua ohasava'ekue juiciope jasypoteĩ ary 2010pe ojeacuságui falsificación, abuso de confianza ha uso indebido computadora rehegua. Kerviel oĩ kuri de acuerdo oipurúhague computadora vai, ha katu i-abogado yma guare, Olivier Metzner, ojerure umi juradope toipe'a Kervielpe abuso de confianza ha falsificación. Metzner he'i kuri CNNpe mba'éichapa oiko Société Généralepe ogueraha vai Kervielpe. 'Umi banco, ndaha'éi Jerome Kerviel, oñekulpáva va'erã sistema bancario ha jehasa asy económico oikóva jey jey rehe,' he'i. Metzner ojapo kuri apelación, ha katu Kerviel omyengovia chupe Koubbi ndive jasyapýpe. Koubbi ojahe'o ndaikatúigui 'opaichagua evidencia pyahu oñemoĩramo jepe,' Kerviel apelación ndohupytýi. Kerviel onegosia kuri umi índice futuro europeo bancope guarã. Ha'e he'i hembiapo ojapo hague i-superior kuéra oikuaáva, ha ha'e ha'eño oñekulpáva. 'Che añemoĩ porãiterei pe kuatia rehe ojehechaukáva che superior kuéra oikuaa ha cheñangareko hague. Ndaha'éi chéve añópe ojehusga va'erã,' omombe'u CNNpe hembiapokue ojekuaa rire, 'Atrapado en una espiral: Memorias de un Trader,' odefendévo isensilles. 'Ko'ã encargado kuéra ogana pirapire hetaiterei umi bono rupive oguejýva umi ganancia are guivéma ame'ẽva bancope,' he'i avei. Societe Generale he'i umi supervisor ndoikuaái hague Kerviel rembiapo vai ojekuaa ramo guare pe pérdida jasyteĩ ary 2008pe. CNN pegua Dheepthi Namasivayam, Sybile Penhirin ha Pierre Meilhan oipytyvõ ko kuatia ojeguatávo.

article_content: The UK Supreme Court upheld the ban on prisoners voting, a decision David Cameron hailed as 'common sense'. Convicted murderers Peter Chester and George McGeoch failed in their attempt to overturn the voting ban. The UK's highest court highlighted widespread public opposition to granting prisoners the right to vote, noting that MPs have actively worked to prevent such a change. Despite the European Court of Human Rights ruling a blanket ban unlawful, the UK government is considering different approaches to determine prisoner voting eligibility. Labour's Sadiq Khan affirmed the party's long-standing policy that prisoners should not have the right to vote.

article_content: In Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, a thief committed a robbery while bizarrely disguised with a plastic bag over his head, having cut out holes for his eyes. This incident happened at a Day One store located in Bennetts Gate. Security footage captured the peculiar raid, during which the man, wearing a white Londis plastic bag, threatened a lone female shop assistant. The crime took place on May 9th at approximately 8:45 am. The suspect is still at large, and police are now releasing the CCTV footage to the public in hopes of identifying him. The video reveals the man entering the store and heading towards the wine section while another customer was being served. Once that customer left, the bag-wearing robber brandished a knife, demanding money from the till. After grabbing an undisclosed amount of cash, he quickly fled the scene. Thankfully, the shop worker was unharmed, though understandably shaken. Despite efforts, law enforcement has yet to apprehend the suspect. To aid in the investigation, the robbery was highlighted on a recent episode of the BBC's Crimewatch program. DC Paula Mowbray of the Hemel Hempstead Police Station's Local Crime Unit described the event as upsetting for the store owner and emphasized their ongoing efforts to identify the perpetrator. She noted the unusual disguise and the visibility of parts of his face, expressing hope that someone would recognize him from the released footage. She urged anyone with information to contact the police at 101, referencing crime number D1/14/2764, or to anonymously contact Crimestoppers at 0800 555 111. Online viewers reacted with amusement to the Herts Police Facebook post about the incident. Comments included humorous takes on the robber's choice of disguise and the desperation implied by his actions.

article_content: By Jill Reilly Published: 12:12 EST, November 23, 2013 Updated: 12:56 EST, November 23, 2013 Latvia's president described the supermarket roof collapse, which killed at least 54 people, as 'murder'. Rescuers searched for as many as 10 more victims believed to be buried in the rubble. Early reports suggested the roof collapsed due to either faulty construction or building work on its grass and gravel-covered surface, where workers were installing a garden area and a children's playground for an adjacent high-rise residential building. Today, Latvia's child welfare department revealed that 16 children had lost parents in the accident, and three of them lost both parents. Tragic: Rescuers searched this morning for 10 missing people who may have been killed in the collapse of a supermarket roof, a disaster which the nation's president described as 'murder'. Cause: Early reports suggest the roof collapsed due to either faulty construction or building work on its grass and gravel-covered surface. Orphans: Laila Rieksta-Riekstina, head of the state's child welfare department, told Latvia Radio that 16 children lost parents in the accident. Three of them lost both parents. President Andris Berzins spoke bluntly about the disaster at the Maxima supermarket in Riga, though he did not single anyone out as culpable. 'This is a case where we need to say clearly it is the murder of an enormous number of defenseless people, and that's how we should proceed,' Mr. Berzins said in an interview with Latvian television. Mr. Berzins called for a speedy investigation to prevent those responsible from covering up a paper trail and 'coming off as pure as angels.' Fifty-four deaths had been confirmed from the structural failure by Saturday afternoon. Police spokesman Dairis Anucins said earlier that there were reports of 10 missing people, and it was not clear if the new death toll included any of them. Token of remembrance: Paintings and flowers are fixed on a fence near the accident site. Grief: Passersby react outside the destroyed Maxima supermarket. Mourning: Latvians streamed to the site in a densely populated neighborhood between downtown Riga and the airport to lay flowers and light candles. Respect: Candles and flowers are laid in front of the Maxima supermarket in Riga. Tragedy: People gather near the collapsed supermarket. Some 40 people were injured, including 13 firefighters who rushed to the scene, and 23 people remained hospitalized as of Saturday afternoon, police said. It was the worst accident in the Baltic country since it regained independence in 1991. The government declared three days of mourning starting Saturday. Latvians streamed to the site in a densely populated neighborhood between downtown Riga and the airport to lay flowers and light candles. Fatal: Large sections of roof collapsed during the evening shopping rush hour. Search: Rescue workers had stopped the operation early Saturday to consult with engineers before continuing. Work: Local media said workers had been building a roof garden on the store, a single-storey building located in a Riga suburb about a 30-minute drive from the city center. Horror: Witnesses said there was a loud noise and the store went dark. People escaped through holes in the windows. Mourning: The government has declared three days of mourning. The Fire and Rescue Service said only 80 square meters (850 square feet) of debris remained to be searched as of late Saturday afternoon, but they said it was a difficult section with rubble piled up to 4 metres (12 feet) high. Rescue workers had stopped the operation early Saturday to consult with engineers before continuing. Pictures show that a large amount of building materials, including bags of soil for the garden, were left in areas of the roof that Riga city officials say could have been vulnerable to heavy loads. Police have launched an investigation, which could take several weeks to complete. Riga Mayor Nils Usakovs wrote on his Twitter account Saturday that once the investigation is over, the supermarket ruins would be razed and a monument built to the victims. He also suggested that the incomplete residential building might be torn down. Remembrance: Latvian President Andris Berzins (second right) and Latvian Parliament Speaker Solvita Aboltina (left) light candles during a service for Maxima supermarket roof collapse victims at Dom Church in Riga.

article_content: On Sunday, two tornadoes struck suburban Washington, D.C., the National Weather Service confirmed. The storms uprooted trees and stripped siding from several homes. Fortunately, no injuries were immediately reported. The first tornado touched down in St. Charles, Maryland, approximately 30 miles south of Washington, D.C., just after 2 p.m. Several trees were uprooted, with many falling onto cars and homes. The strongest winds from this tornado reached 80 mph, strong enough to break windows. About 30 minutes later, a second tornado occurred outside Hyattsville, Maryland, roughly 10 miles northeast of the capital. Peak winds of 100 mph severely impacted the George E. Peters Adventist School, tearing off part of its roof and scattering debris into the parking lot. A nearby construction trailer was also overturned.

article_content: Amid the escalating conflict in Somalia, the nation's president has appealed to Somali expatriates in the United States, urging them to dissuade their sons from joining the fighting. A Somali rebel is pictured with a heavy machine gun aimed towards government forces on July 3. 'I implore the Somali-American community to prevent their youth from enlisting with al-Shabaab in Somalia,' stated President Sheik Sharif Ahmed on Sunday. He was referencing the Islamist militant organization engaged in a violent conflict against his administration in Mogadishu. 'To those young men abroad, I say: Your families sought refuge in America due to insecurity. Do not return to incite violence against your own people,' he urged. Significant numbers of Somalis began immigrating to the United States following the U.S. intervention in Somalia's humanitarian crisis in 1992. Last year, a considerable group of young Somali-American men departed from Minneapolis, raising concerns about their potential recruitment by al-Shabaab militants. In October, Shirwa Ahmed, a 27-year-old Somali-American radicalized by al-Shabaab in Minnesota, his adopted state, carried out a suicide bombing in Somalia, killing himself and 29 others. This incident, marking the first suicide attack by a naturalized U.S. citizen, triggered alarms within the U.S. intelligence community. The president's appeal followed renewed clashes on Sunday between Somalia's transitional government forces and Islamist insurgents. Eyewitness accounts indicate that AMISOM (the African Union Mission to Somalia) supported government forces in repelling al-Shabaab's assault on the presidential palace. Witnesses reported the involvement of AMISOM tanks and soldiers in the hostilities. 'The intense sound of heavy artillery in Mogadishu was constant and deafening,' a witness reported to CNN. 'The ground trembled, and numerous buildings were decimated by the shelling.' The president hailed the operation as 'a decisive victory' against al-Shabaab. 'Our forces have significantly weakened al-Shabaab's strength in this engagement,' Ahmed stated. Government forces displayed the remains of five al-Shabaab fighters clad in their distinctive green uniforms. Al-Shabaab, an organization designated as a terror group by the U.S. government, maintains a stronghold in the northeast and parts of southern Mogadishu. The group characterized AMISOM's involvement as a turning point in their efforts to overthrow the transitional government. 'The fighting in Mogadishu has entered a new stage. It is now a direct confrontation between us and AMISOM,' stated Ali Mohamud Rage, an al-Shabaab spokesman. 'AMISOM directly supported the government, but we will continue our fight.' Somalia has been in turmoil since 1991, when warlords ousted dictator Mohamed Siad Barre, leading to internecine clan warfare. The transitional government has struggled to establish control, facing challenges from Islamist groups that have seized control of Mogadishu and much of the southern region. The United Nations estimates that over 200,000 people have been displaced from Mogadishu since the latest outbreak of fighting between the government and Al-Shabaab and Hisb-ul-Islam began in early May. The Somali-American population in the United States is largely concentrated in Minneapolis; Columbus, Ohio; Seattle, Washington; and San Diego, California. The potential recruitment of young Somali-American men is facilitated by 'a confluence of factors, including a dynamic, influential, and extremist leader gaining access to a despondent and disenfranchised group of young men,' according to Andrew Liepman, deputy director for intelligence at the National Counterterrorism Center, earlier this year. Many refugees, he noted, 'lack structure and purpose in their lives' and are 'caught between the traditional tribal and clan identities of their parents and the new cultures and traditions offered by American society.'

article_content: Katy Winter reports that a new tearoom in Weston-super-Mare, named The Blitz Tearoom, transports visitors back to wartime Britain. This unique cafe aims to recreate the atmosphere of the 1940s through its music, featuring artists like Glenn Miller and Vera Lynn, as well as its decor, menu, and staff uniforms, all reminiscent of World War II. Michelle Austin, an ex-army corporal, established The Blitz Tearoom to celebrate the spirit of the Blitz. The cafe showcases 1940s relics, including antique tins that once contained dried milk, camp coffee, and anti-gas ointment, alongside Blitz-era radiograms and Bakelite phones. The walls are painted a 1940s-typical mint green, and wartime memorabilia such as gas masks, home guard training manuals, and ration book-covered menus are on display. Michelle has transformed the corridor into a replica of Bethnal Green underground station, which served as an air raid shelter during the war. Michelle, 37, served in Germany before leaving the army in 2004 after nine years. Seeking a new challenge, she initially worked in kitchen assistant roles but found them unfulfilling. She then trained as a chef and worked in a tearoom, which inspired her to create her own establishment. After finding a suitable premise, a former clothes shop, the transformation took a year of hard work. Michelle expressed her delight with the final result. The walls are adorned with Union Jack bunting, flags, and images of Lancaster Bombers and Spitfires, along with posters displaying wartime slogans like 'Dig for Victory' and 'Make do and Mend'. A British flag hangs on the wall, accompanied by a painting depicting German planes bombing London during the Blitz. The menu offers a 1940s culinary experience, featuring retro finger sandwiches with fillings like spam, egg and cress, and corned beef. Michelle and her staff wear authentic polka dot dresses, headscarves, and floral aprons. A War Department sign reading 'When in doubt, brew up' is displayed at the counter, alongside other wartime messages. Michelle is thrilled with the tearoom's transformation, which includes a Welsh dresser filled with vintage crockery. The corridor leading to the courtyard is designed to resemble Bethnal Green underground station, complete with posters from the era. Mannequins dressed as a woman and a child evacuee complete the scene. The menu includes 1940s-style dishes and drinks such as milk served in old-fashioned glass bottles, ginger beer, and Camp coffee. Michelle says she's always been interested in retro themes and plans to host World War II-themed nights.

Ko café ijupeguáva oha'ãrõ omoheñói jey umi ary 1940-pe guarégui imúsica rupive, oguerúvo artista kuéra Glenn Miller ha Vera Lynn-pe, avei idécora, menú ha umi funcionario ao, opaiteva'ekue ogueromandu'áva Segunda Guerra Mundial. Michelle Austin, peteĩ ex-ejército korporál, omoheñói The Blitz Tearoom omomorã haguã pe Blitz espíritu. article_content: Detroit, Michigan, Police Chief Warren Evans resigned on Wednesday, according to a city announcement. Mayor Dave Bing stated, 'We appreciate the time and dedication that Warren Evans has given to the Detroit Police Department. He has put the department on a path to reducing crime.' The mayor appointed Assistant Chief Ralph Godbee as interim police chief. At a news conference, Bing said, 'I received information regarding some issues within our police department. I believe Chief Evans' decisions compromised his position, leading to my decision to replace him.' Bing declined to elaborate on the specific decisions that led to Evans' resignation, stating only that the move resulted from internal and external feedback collected over time. 'It's a combination of several factors,' Bing said. Evans faced scrutiny in May after allowing a reality film crew to accompany officers executing a search warrant for a murder suspect, WDIV, a CNN affiliate, reported. During that incident, an officer was accused of fatally shooting a 7-year-old girl inside the home. WDIV reported that Evans became the third Detroit police chief within a year when he took office last summer. Godbee said, 'We've made significant strides in the police department using a data-driven approach to solving crime. We will continue to build on the successes we are achieving.'

article_content: Ukrainian soldiers told the Kyiv Independent they are worried about running out of combat-capable personnel to continue fighting against Russia as the war continues. In a report published on Thursday, multiple soldiers fighting in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk Oblast said that it was becoming increasingly difficult to achieve a major breakthrough in the area. While Russia continues to send ammunition and large numbers of troops to replenish the front lines, Ukrainian soldiers said they were worried about how long they will be able to sustain the pace of the war. 'If combat-capable people like us run out, we could only be replaced by people who don't know anything,' Roman, who has been serving since 2016, told the Kyiv Independent. A driver, deployed with the 92nd Separate Assault Brigade near Bakhmut, also told the publication that he was worried about the possibility of the country running out of experienced and motivated soldiers. 'We're already running out of people,' the driver, whose call sign is 'Ninja,' said. 'The war will be very, very long.' Ukraine has not released official death toll figures, but US officials told The New York Times in August that the number likely stands at approximately 500,000. Oleksandr Maroshnyk, a 31-year-old infantryman from Odesa who also served with the 93rd Separate Mechanized Brigade, told the Kyiv Independent that of the original 110 people serving in his unit in June 2022, only four remain in action because everyone else was either dead or injured. 'You can't imagine what we endured because, imagine, killing from morning to evening – it's terrible,' he said. Maroshnyk was fighting mostly in Bakhmut. Losing friends on the front lines and spending up to 13 hours a day in the trenches is also taking a heavy toll on the mental health of Ukrainian soldiers, who told the Kyiv Independent they are feeling increasingly burned out. One infantryman from the 28th Separate Mechanized Brigade told the outlet that while he is not afraid of dying himself, he is shocked by the number of friends he has already lost. 'I just want to go home, I'm so tired,' the 41-year-old soldier, identified only as Anatoly, told the outlet. 'When will this fucking war end? How many more friends killed do I need?'

article_content: A Greek investigative journalist was acquitted of criminal charges on Thursday after publishing the names of approximately 2,000 Greeks holding Swiss bank accounts, a disclosure that proved embarrassing for the nation's political and business leaders. Kostas Vaxevanis, editor of Hot Doc magazine, faced charges for violating Greece's data protection law. He was arrested on Sunday, a day after his magazine released the list, and acquitted Thursday night, according to his defense attorney, Harris Ikonomopoulos. The names were dubbed the 'Lagarde list,' as they originated from Christine Lagarde, then France's finance minister, who provided them to her Greek counterpart in August 2010. Lagarde now heads the International Monetary Fund. Vaxevanis defended his publication, arguing that the data came from a reliable source and its release was in the public interest. 'In the past two years, various names have been bandied about,' he told reporters outside the courthouse on Thursday. 'People have been blackmailed. Fake lists have circulated. The political system is being destabilized. A fabricated list even included half of the Greek lawmakers' names. Doesn't this situation warrant intervention?' While possessing a Swiss bank account isn't illegal, and no evidence indicates any lawbreaking, there's widespread suspicion in Greece that some individuals on the list may have opened accounts to evade Greek taxes. Greek media questioned whether the failure to investigate those named for potential tax evasion resulted from politicians protecting a wealthy elite. A parliamentary committee is investigating why no inquiry was initiated under either former Finance Minister George Papaconstantinou or his successor, Evangelos Venizelos. The ministers claimed the data was given to the fraud office, but officials there denied ever receiving formal instructions to investigate the list's members for tax avoidance. French and German authorities, also given similar lists, pursued some individuals named for alleged tax evasion. Greek authorities now face public scrutiny for allegedly targeting the journalist, Vaxevanis, while seemingly ignoring the list for two years. Ikonomopoulos stated his client should have been commended for his courage in revealing the list instead of being prosecuted. 'The Greek government needs to investigate this list and any other lists they may possess,' Ikonomopoulos told CNN. 'But crucially, the Greek government must reinstate effective governance, checks and balances, and accountability and transparency mechanisms to ensure any action is productive,' he added. 'We can no longer tolerate injustice, mismanagement, or lies that tarnish public life and delegitimize public personnel at a time when collaboration is essential.'

Kostas Vaxevanis, editor revista Hot Doc-pegua, oñemoĩ kuri proceso-pe violando Grecia léi de protección de datos rehegua. Ojejagarra chupe domingo-pe, peteĩ ára rire irrevista osẽ rire pe lista, ha oje absolve chupe jueves pyharépe, he’iháicha abogado defensor, Harris Ikonomopoulos. Umi téra ojekuaa “Lista Lagarde” ramo, ougui Christine Lagarde-gui, upérõ ministra de finanzas Francia-pegua, ome’ẽva’ekue imbojaojára griego-pe agosto 2010-pe. Ko’ág̃a Lagarde omyakã Fondo Monetario Internacional-pe. Vaxevanis odefende ipublicación, he’ívo umi dato ou hague fuente confiable-gui ha pe divulgación oĩ hague interés público-pe. ‘Umi mokõi ary pahápe, heta téra osẽ osyryry’, he’i periodista-kuérape okápe tribunal-gui jueves-pe. ‘Oĩ tapicha oje chantajeáva. Peteĩ lista inventada-pe jepe oĩ kuri media cantidad umi legislador griego téra. ¿Ndaikatumo’ãi piko ojejoko ko situación?’ Ndaipóri mba’eve ivaíva orekóramo cuenta bancaria Suiza-pe, ha ndaipóri mba’eve ohechaukáva oje violahague léi, heta oĩ ogueroviáva Grecia-pe oĩha umi lista-pe oipe’áva cuenta omboye hag̃ua impuesto Grecia-pe. Umi medio de comunicación griego oñeporandu mba’épa ndoje investigái umi téra oje’éva ododgahague impuesto, ha péva ikatúne político-kuéra oproteheségui umi ricoitépe. Peteĩ comisión parlamentaria oinvestiga mba’érepa ndojejapói kuri investigación ex Ministro de Finanzas George Papaconstantinou térã isucesor, Evangelos Venizelos poguýpe. Umi autoridad francesa ha alemana, oñeme’ẽva’ekue avei chupekuéra lista ojoguáva, omboja’o kuri umi téra he’íva ododgahague impuesto. Umi autoridad griega ko’ág̃a ho’a hína héra vaiete umi tapicha renondépe oje’égui oataka hague periodista Vaxevanis-pe, ha oje’éma voi mokõi ary ojeguapy hague pe lista ári ha ndojejapói mba’eve. Ikonomopoulos he’i icliente oñemomba’eguasúva’erã kuri pe py’aguasu orekóre omosarambi hag̃ua pe lista ha ndaha’éi ojegueraha chupe tribunal-pe. ‘Gobierno griego oinvestigava’erã ko lista ha ambue lista orekóva ipópe’, he’i Ikonomopoulos CNN-pe. ‘Ha katu, iprincipalvéva, gobierno griego omoĩ jeyva’erã en vigencia peteĩ gobernanza efectiva, umi control ha equilibrio, ha umi mecanismo de rendición de cuentas ha transparencia, ikatu hag̃uáicha oimeháicha acción iproductivo’, he’i avei. ‘Ndaikatuvéi jaaguanta injusticia, mala gestión, térã japu omongy’áva tekovévape ha omboguejýva credibilidad umi funcionario público-pe peteĩ tiempo-pe ñaikotevẽhápe jajapo servicio joajupe’.
